meta.title: Guided decision flow (questionnaire)

modes.quick: Quick questions only; everything else takes its default
modes.any: reference panel, available on every screen, never required

meta.time_weight_rule: high: a decided card has fan-out 5+ or the question is Quick; medium: fan-out 2-4, or an asset hook, input question, the reference panel, or block class I; low: otherwise

interview_protocol: Agree the mode (quick, standard, expert). Offer the reference panel (Q-ref-01) and keep it open.
Walk stages in order. Open each with one sentence on what it decides; render its preview if the host can show visuals, else describe the example in words.
Ask each question whose modes include the chosen mode and whose show_if holds, using its ask line.

time_weight high: explain why, show 2-3 options with effect and a real system, recommend the default with its source, state what it changes. medium: ask with the default and main alternatives. low: state the default in one line and confirm.
Asset hooks (kind=hook): ask whether the person has the asset, accept hook.accepts formats, otherwise offer hook.if_no paths with their caveats.
Record {question id, option value, set_by: chosen|confirmed_default|auto_default|reference}. Out-of-mode questions take their default.
If an answer conflicts with an earlier one in the same cycle, show the conflict and settle it with the ranked principles (Q-brand-07). Do not average silently.
After each stage, summarize decisions in plain sentences and append them to the decision log for later sessions and teammates.
Only offer listed option values; record anything else as a custom value with the person's reason.

Show on the best surface the host supports (MCP view, canvas or artifact, Figma or Paper via MCP, local HTML, host question tool, plain text); say which is in use; never block on a visual (DC-L18-06).

One question per turn: recommended option plus 2-3 closest alternatives with a visual each, 'other' allowed, one line on what it changes; one high-weight question per turn, up to three low-weight ones grouped; a single form is fine on cycle screens (DC-L18-08, DC-L18-09).

Gates: approve after scope stages 01-05 (with the block map tagged by block_class), after direction stages 06-08, and after the asset checklist; finish with a coverage check. Quick mode keeps only the direction gate (DC-L17-12, DC-L17-09).
Never invent owner-input (block_class I) answers: in Quick mode record meta.quick_mode_assumed_owner_inputs as assumed and list them for confirmation at the end (DC-L17-08).

Write durable outputs to the user's repo: DTCG tokens (canonical), DESIGN.md, an ADR-style decision log, a state file with answers, statuses and coverage, an AGENTS.md pointer, and exported lint rules (DC-L18-10, DC-L18-11).

stages.title: Reference intake (a side panel on every screen)
stages.screen: Not a step in the sequence. The panel sits beside every stage; anything added here is read once and offered as pre-filled answers on the stages that follow, each marked "from reference" until the person confirms it.

stages.title: Scope and team
stages.screen: Screen: what the system is for and who builds it. Graph step 0-2. Cycle kept together: DC-L11-02 + DC-L11-04 (scope decides what to audit; the audit reshapes scope).

stages.title: Audience and commitments
stages.screen: Screen: who the product is for and what it promises them. Graph step 0. These answers bound every later option.

stages.title: Brand personality and principles
stages.screen: Screen: who the brand is, and which brand assets already exist. Graph step 0-1. Personality has the largest fan-out in the graph (15 decisions), so it comes before any foundation [DC-L06-02]. The grouped asset checklist (Q-brand-08) sits here, as L17 recommends, so missing assets can be commissioned while the rest of the flow continues [DC-L17-04].

stages.title: Platforms and devices
stages.screen: Screen: where the product runs and what people touch it with. Graph step 0-2. Cycle kept together: DC-L10-01 + DC-L10-02 + DC-L10-03 + DC-L10-21 (platforms, posture, sharing layer and framework constrain each other). Placed after personality so the posture default can come from slider G [inferred; DC-L06-14 depends on DC-L06-02].

stages.title: Where the system lives
stages.screen: Screen: design tool, source of truth and how engineers consume the output. Graph step 0-1. Asked before any foundation because it decides what the builder generates on every later preview [DC-L16-02]. The design-tool plan comes first because it limits where the source of truth can live (Figma REST writes need Enterprise) [DC-L07-27, DC-L07-08].

stages.title: Visual direction
stages.screen: Screen: the overall look before any single foundation. Graph step 2-3. Cycle kept together: DC-L15-01 (style preset) + DC-L15-04 (density voice): a minimal style needs low density to stay usable, and a dense layout needs a style with strong signifiers [DC-L15-01, DC-L15-04; S-L15-004]. Quick mode derives every answer here from Q-aud-01 and the personality sliders.

stages.title: Themes and modes
stages.screen: Screen: which variations of the system exist. Graph step 0-2. Asked before color because every color decision must be made once per mode [DC-L07-15; BOARD L01 note: dark mode is always a separate mapping].

stages.title: Color system
stages.screen: Screen: one screen with four sections (brand input, strategy, ramps and neutrals, roles and contrast) around one shared live preview: a product screen, the generated ramps, and a contrast matrix of every foreground/background pair, in light and dark. Graph step 1-4. Cycle kept together: the 21-card color cycle (DC-L01-01 to DC-L01-13, DC-L01-15, DC-L01-18, DC-L01-21 to DC-L01-24, DC-L15-03, DC-L15-06) plus the two-card cycle DC-L10-04 + DC-L10-05. Changing any answer here regenerates the whole palette, so the questions share one preview instead of separate screens [inferred from the cycle].

stages.title: Color details and accessibility modes
stages.screen: Screen: the fine-grained color roles that follow from Stage 08, on the same live preview. Graph step 5-6. Mostly Expert; Standard asks only about hover feel and dark-mode darkness.

stages.title: Typeface
stages.screen: Screen: which fonts, for which scripts. Graph step 2-4. Cycles kept together: DC-L02-01 + DC-L02-02 + DC-L02-03 + DC-L02-04 + DC-L02-06 + DC-L02-24 (the typeface must cover your scripts and license terms, and those in turn narrow the typeface) and DC-L06-07 + DC-L06-24 (brand typeface vs localization readiness). The preview is a type specimen in the product's own UI, with a coverage bar for each chosen script.

stages.title: Type scale and text
stages.screen: Screen: sizes, line heights, weights and text behavior, on a live type ladder next to a real product screen. Graph step 0-5. Cycle kept together: DC-L02-13 + DC-L02-25 (line heights must fit each script's height category, and script metrics are set relative to the line-height system). Mostly pre-filled from Q-aud-01 (density) and Q-dir-03 (hierarchy strength).

stages.title: Space, sizing and density
stages.screen: Screen: the spacing scale, target sizes and control heights, shown on a live component sheet with spacing overlays (padding in one tint, gaps in another). Graph step 0-6. Pre-filled from Q-aud-01, Q-plat-03 and Q-dir-02.

stages.title: Layout, navigation and app shell
stages.screen: Screen: how pages reorganize across widths, shown on a resizable frame the person can drag from phone to wide desktop. Graph step 0-4. Safe areas and edge insets (DC-L03-20, DC-L14-10) are not asked; they are platform rules applied by construction (see "Auto-applied rules").

stages.title: Shape
stages.screen: Screen: corner radius, on a live component sheet (button, input, card, dialog, menu, avatar, image). Graph step 1-5. The signature-shape question comes first because brand shape language drives the roundness dial (graph-overrides.json edge DC-L06-09 to DC-L04-02). Nested radii follow the concentric rule automatically (DC-L04-05, see "Auto-applied rules").

stages.title: Depth, borders and materials
stages.screen: Screen: how surfaces separate and float, on a live stack (page, card, menu, dialog, sheet over a photo) in light and dark. Graph step 0-4. Cycle kept together: DC-L10-11 + DC-L10-12 (edge-to-edge content under the system bars decides the bar material, and the material decides how bars treat content beneath them). Layer order (z-index) and opaque fallbacks for translucency are applied by construction (see "Auto-applied rules").

stages.title: Motion, haptics and sound
stages.screen: Screen: motion feel on live interactions the person can trigger (open a menu, navigate, toggle, dismiss a sheet), with a reduced-motion toggle. Graph step 0-6.

stages.title: Icons, app icon and logo use
stages.screen: Screen: an icon sheet in the product's own buttons, tabs and lists, next to body text at each size. Graph step 0-4. Two asset hooks live here: the icon set (Q-icon-01) and the app icon (Q-icon-06).

stages.title: Imagery, illustration and charts
stages.screen: Screen: an empty state, onboarding card, hero and dashboard, with the person's own assets dropped in where they exist. Graph step 0-3. Three asset hooks live here: photography (Q-img-01), illustration (Q-img-04) and animated assets (Q-img-06). Image placeholders, chart anatomy tokens and chart accessibility are applied by construction (see "Auto-applied rules").

stages.title: Content and voice
stages.screen: Screen: the product's own buttons, errors, empty states and a success message, rewritten live as voice and tone settings change. Graph step 1-3. Voice comes before components because every component ships its microcopy rules (L06: "voice is a foundation, not a docs appendix") [DC-L06-18]. One asset hook: an existing voice guide (Q-voice-01).

stages.title: Component base and inventory
stages.screen: Screen: the component catalog, rendered with every foundation chosen so far; each component opens to a detail card (anatomy, states, when to use, when not to use). Graph step 0-3.

stages.title: Actions, states and focus
stages.screen: Screen: a live component sheet where every control can be hovered, pressed, focused with the keyboard, disabled and set to loading. Graph step 0-7. The microinteraction spec (DC-L13-12) is generated for every component (see "Auto-applied rules").

stages.title: Forms, validation and feedback
stages.screen: Screen: a live sign-up form and a list with delete actions; the person fills fields, triggers errors and deletes items to feel each option. Graph step 0-6. Cycles kept together: DC-L08-10 + DC-L08-17 (whether submit can be disabled depends on when validation runs, and vice versa), DC-L13-06 + DC-L13-07 (timing and error message pattern), DC-L13-08 + DC-L13-09 (undo needs a channel such as a toast; the channel set depends on whether undo exists).

stages.title: Patterns and AI surfaces
stages.screen: Screen: small flows the person can click through: open a dialog and a side sheet, page through a table, reach an empty state, meet a consent prompt, and see AI-generated content. Graph step 0-2. Content hierarchy for scanning (DC-L13-04) is applied by construction.

stages.title: Tokens and encoding
stages.screen: Screen: a token browser beside the product preview; clicking any element shows its token chain (component, semantic, primitive) and the exported code for each platform. Graph step 0-5. Asked after the visual stages because nothing visual depends on it in the graph; everything here changes how the look is stored and shipped [inferred from the graph].

stages.title: Team, governance and change
stages.screen: Screen: a governance plan generated from earlier answers (team size, scope, platforms), shown as a one-page operating model the person edits. Graph step 1-7. Mostly Expert: these decisions change how the system evolves, not how it looks.

stages.title: Output, documentation and AI channels
stages.screen: Screen: the export menu and a preview of every file the builder will produce: tokens, code, docs pages, DESIGN.md, lint rules. Graph step 2-4. These outputs are what keep the system coherent in later sessions and explainable to a team (BRIEF requirements 9 and 10).

stages.title: Builder preferences
stages.screen: Screen: how the builder (or the interviewing model) behaves while the person keeps editing. Graph step 0-5. Can be changed at any time.

questions.question: Do you have a website, screenshot, Figma file or other example to learn from?

options.label: A live website URL
options.effect: the builder reads computed colors, type, spacing, radius, shadows, motion and components [inferred; S-L16-405].

options.label: Screenshots or images
options.effect: color, type size ratios, density, radius and depth are estimated from pixels; values are marked as estimates [inferred].

options.label: A Figma file or library
options.effect: variables, styles and components are read through the Figma MCP (`get_variable_defs`, `get_design_context`, `get_screenshot`) [DC-L11-23; S-L11-041].

options.label: Your code, a CSS file or a token JSON file
options.effect: exact values, including DTCG files [DC-L07-08; S-L07-011].

options.label: A brand book, voice guide or PDF
options.effect: brand colors, typefaces, voice traits [inferred].

questions.ask: Is there a site, screenshot or Figma file whose structure or quality you like? I'll read it and suggest answers.
questions.example: Ask for a URL of their own product or an app they admire; show the 'extracted from reference' card with 3-4 found values.
questions.why: A reference lets the builder suggest answers, so you don't start from a blank page. Tools do this now: Google Stitch reads a design system from a URL, and Polymet pulls tokens from one [S-L16-256, S-L16-405].
questions.control: drop zone + URL field; multiple references allowed, each tagged "our product", "inspiration" or "competitor"
questions.default: none
questions.preview: an "extracted from reference" card listing each found value next to the question it would answer, with Accept, Adjust and Ignore buttons.
questions.use_avoid: use a reference to copy structure and quality (spacing rhythm, type ratios, density, depth model); avoid copying another brand's identity: its logo, brand color, proprietary typeface or illustration are never carried over, and a "competitor" reference is used only to flag shared tropes [BRIEF requirement 4; S-L06-027].

questions.question: Which products and pages should this system cover, and which should it leave out?

options.label: Product app
options.effect: tight, opinionated visuals are possible when this is the only surface [DC-L11-02, inferred].

options.label: Marketing site
options.effect: adds an expressive layer next to the productive one (Carbon splits productive and expressive type and motion) [DC-L06-01; S-L06-001].

options.label: Internal or admin tools
options.effect: usually dense (see Q-aud-01) [inferred].

options.label: Docs or content site
options.effect: long-form reading pushes line length and paragraph rules (DC-L02-17) [inferred].

options.label: Email
options.effect: a constrained rendering target the token pipeline must also output [DC-L11-02 options].

options.label: Inside partner sites or apps
options.effect: need scoped, context-agnostic components ("card", not "product card") [S-L11-002].

questions.ask: Is this only for your app, or also your marketing site, docs, emails or in-house tools?
questions.example: Show two thumbnails, an app screen and a marketing page, drawn from the same tokens.
questions.why: What the system covers sets how general your components must be. It also sets how many layers of design tokens you need [DC-L11-02].
questions.default: product-app only
questions.default_source: card heuristic, scope v1 to what the pilot touches [DC-L11-02; S-L11-083].
questions.preview: a strip with one sample screen per selected surface, all rendered from the same draft tokens.
questions.skip: yes, defaults to a single product app.

questions.question: Is there existing UI to clean up and merge, or is this a new product?

options.label: New product
options.effect: skip the audit and go straight to visual language [S-L11-105].

options.label: Existing screens, sorted by hand
options.effect: screenshots across 16 categories, then keep/merge/kill decisions (Brad Frost) [S-L11-001].

options.label: Existing screens, counted by a tool
options.effect: unique colors and declarations (CSS Stats), component and prop usage (Omlet, react-scanner), Figma library analytics [S-L11-105, S-L11-037, S-L11-039, S-L11-035].

options.label: Both
options.effect: automated counts plus the manual inventory for shared vocabulary [DC-L11-04 default].

questions.ask: Do you have screens already that we should clean up and merge, or are we starting fresh?
questions.example: If existing, ask for a URL or CSS file; show a count like '38 grays, 14 button styles found'.
questions.why: Checking the screens you have (an audit) shows how much to merge. For example, 40 grays can merge into one 10-step color ramp [DC-L11-04, inferred].
questions.control: single choice (+ URL or CSS import when existing)
questions.default: greenfield; if existing UI, `both`
questions.default_source: card heuristic, the manual inventory's main value is shared vocabulary and buy-in [DC-L11-04; S-L11-001].
questions.preview: an inventory board: counts of unique colors, type styles and button variants found, with the proposed consolidated ramp beside them.

questions.question: Who will use the system itself?

options.label: Engineers
options.effect: component API docs and code packages (DC-L11-18).

options.label: Designers
options.effect: a design-tool library (DC-L16-13).

options.label: Writers and people in product or marketing
options.effect: usage and voice guidance (DC-L06-18).

options.label: External partners
options.effect: public docs and stricter versioning (DC-L11-14).

options.label: AI coding agents
options.effect: MCP server, DESIGN.md, llms.txt (12 of 25 benchmarked systems ship one) [L09 A1 row 10; DC-L11-23].

questions.ask: Who will work with the system: engineers, designers, writers, partners, or AI tools that write code?
questions.example: Show the output list per audience, e.g. 'AI agents get DESIGN.md and an MCP manifest'.
questions.why: Each group that uses the system needs its own docs and file formats. AI coding agents need files a machine can read [DC-L11-02; S-L11-083].
questions.default: engineers + designers + ai-agents
questions.default_source: L09 shared pattern row 10 (agent-readable exports in 12 of 25 systems) [inferred choice].
questions.preview: a list of the output files the builder will generate for each checked audience.

questions.question: How many people will build and look after the system, and how do they work together?

options.label: 1-2 people (28% of teams) [S-L11-030].
One team, for itself
options.effect: one team makes it for itself and shares it (Curtis) [S-L11-005].

options.label: One central team
options.effect: a dedicated team serves product teams [S-L11-005].

options.label: Shared by several teams
options.effect: designers from several product teams decide together [S-L11-005].

options.label: Central team plus helpers
options.effect: central librarian team plus federated contributors (Salesforce) [S-L11-013].

questions.ask: How many people will build and look after this, and are they one team or spread across product teams?
questions.example: Give the survey split: most teams are 1-5 people.
questions.why: Team size sets how much the builder must do for you. Small teams should adapt an accessible base that exists, not build from scratch [DC-L11-01, DC-L11-10].
questions.default: 1-2 people, centralized with a named owner
questions.preview: none visual; shows which governance defaults (contribution flow, review gates) the builder will switch on.

questions.question: What are you starting from: a product you have, a UI kit, a site you like, or only a brief?

options.label: From an existing product
options.effect: audit and extract, then consolidate (the interface inventory; see Q-scope-02) [DC-L17-02; DC-L11-04].

options.label: From a UI kit or library (Untitled UI, Material 3 kit, shadcn)
options.effect: fast, but the kit's defaults become the look unless changed (the M3 kit shipped 6 versions in 12 months) [DC-L17-02; S-L17-322].

options.label: From a reference you admire
options.effect: carry structure and quality, never identity (gstack and Stitch support this) [DC-L17-02; S-L17-003].

options.label: From a brief only
options.effect: interview, then generate directions [DC-L17-02; S-L17-021].

options.label: Use as is, adapt, or build your own
options.effect: adopt a system as-is (Material, Carbon, Fluent), adapt a themeable base (shadcn create, Radix Themes), or create your own; NN/g ranks their cost lowest to highest [DC-L11-01; S-L11-006, S-L11-071, S-L11-068].

options.label: How close to stay to the reference
options.effect: reinterpret the lessons (default), replicate structure with every identity element swapped (only for "our version of this"), or read a competitor only to list shared tropes; copying identity is never offered [DC-L17-03; S-L17-023, S-L17-022].

questions.ask: Where do we start: your product, a UI kit, a site you admire, or a blank page and a brief?
questions.example: Show the same screen started from a stock kit, from a reference's structure with your identity, and from the brief alone.
questions.why: A kit makes your system look like the kit, and a reference passes on its rhythm. A brief gives the widest range of looks but needs the most choices. Using a system as is, adapting one or making your own sets the cost [DC-L17-02, DC-L11-01; S-L11-006].
questions.control: single choice (entry) + single choice (build posture) + single choice (reference fidelity, shown for the reference path)
questions.default: existing product: audit first; otherwise brief first with an optional reference, a kit only as a component base (Q-comp-01), not as the visual direction; small teams adapt an accessible base; references reinterpreted
questions.preview: the three starting points side by side on one screen, with "carried from reference" and "swapped" labels on each element.
questions.use_avoid: use a kit for components and a reference for structure; avoid letting either become the brand ("websites made with shadcn/ui famously look the same") [DC-L11-01; S-L11-073].

questions.question: Who uses the product, and how often?

options.label: All day, in tools full of data
options.effect: body 13-14px, controls 28-32px; compact and utilitarian (Polaris 13px, SLDS 13px, Carbon, Atlassian, Primer, Ant 14px) [DC-L09-04; S-L09-403].

options.label: Often, in an everyday app
options.effect: body 16px, controls 36-40px (Radix, shadcn, Mantine, Chakra) [DC-L09-04; L09 A3 density].

options.label: Now and then, on a phone or in public
options.effect: body 17px or more, controls and targets 44-48px (iOS 17pt, GOV.UK 19px, Material, USWDS 48px targets) [DC-L09-04; S-L09-540].

questions.ask: Who uses it, and how often: all day for work, often, or now and then on the go?
questions.example: Show one table-and-form screen at dense, regular and large densities side by side.
questions.why: Who uses it sets density (how packed the screen is) and base text size. Across systems, body text runs 13-19px. Our L09 study puts this fourth on its list of ways systems look most different (an inferred ranking) [DC-L09-04; L09 A2 row 4].
questions.default: regular
questions.default_source: L09 shared default row 8 (body 16px general, 14px tools) [L09 A1].
questions.preview: the same table-plus-form screen at the three densities side by side; hovering a row shows its height, padding and text size.
questions.use_avoid: use dense for tables, dashboards and editors people work in all day; avoid dense on touch-first, occasional or public surfaces, where it hurts legibility and forces the targets out of step with the visuals [DC-L09-04, DC-L15-04].
questions.skip: yes, defaults to regular. Target sizes do not shrink with density; they follow input precision (Q-space-03, DC-L14-03).

questions.question: What is at stake for users, and what state are they usually in?

options.label: Money, health or government
options.effect: caps expressiveness and playful motion; calm, formal defaults [S-L06-010, S-L06-041].

options.label: Work or business tools
options.effect: productive defaults (Carbon, Atlassian, Primer quadrant) [L09 A3].

options.label: Apps for everyday life
options.effect: room for brand color and hero moments [DC-L06-03].

options.label: Games, fun or learning
options.effect: characters and springs are acceptable (Duolingo, Mailchimp) [S-L06-026, S-L06-027].

options.label: How they feel (pick any)
options.effect: anxious, rushed, curious, celebrating; each shifts the tone matrix (Atlassian tones by emotion) [S-L06-060, S-L06-014].

questions.ask: What's at stake for your users, and how do they usually feel when they use it?
questions.example: Contrast a banking transfer screen with a game reward screen.
questions.why: What's at stake caps how lively the product can be. Google found expressive design may not suit banking [S-L06-010]. How users feel sets the tone [DC-L06-19; S-L06-060].
questions.default: work, states "rushed"
questions.default_source: [inferred]; matches the L09 productive quadrant most benchmarked systems occupy [L09 A3].
questions.preview: a pre-filled position on the personality sliders of Stage 03, with a note where the category caps them.

questions.question: Which set of accessibility rules do you need to meet?

options.label: WCAG 2.2 AA
options.effect: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI parts, 24px target floor (GOV.UK commits to 2.2 AA) [S-L11-093; L09 A1 row 11; DC-L03-12].

options.label: AA plus some AAA rules, like 7:1 body text or bigger targets
options.effect: stricter palettes, fewer mid-tone text colors [DC-L01-22, inferred].

options.label: Level A only
options.effect: not recommended; no benchmarked system states a target below AA [L09 A1 row 11].

questions.ask: How strict do your accessibility rules need to be? WCAG 2.2 has levels A, AA and AAA.
questions.example: Show a text pair that passes 4.5:1 and one that fails.
questions.why: The level you pick sets limits on color, text size, focus rings and target sizes in each later stage [DC-L11-19].
questions.default: WCAG 2.2 AA
questions.default_source: accessibility rule; all 11 benchmarked systems that state a target use AA; WCAG 3 is still a draft, so 2.2 is the enforceable target [L09 A1 row 11; BOARD L01 note].
questions.preview: a guardrail strip listing which later options will be blocked or flagged at this level.
questions.skip: yes, AA. The builder also generates the system-vs-product-team responsibility statement GOV.UK publishes [S-L11-092].

questions.question: Which settings should users be able to adjust, and which situations must you design for?

options.label: Text size
options.effect: layouts must reflow at large sizes (DC-L02-21).

options.label: Compact or roomy switch
options.effect: adds a compact/comfortable token mode (DC-L03-11).

options.label: Contrast themes
options.effect: adds a high-contrast mode (DC-L01-20).

options.label: Reduced motion
options.effect: swaps movement for fades (DC-L04-25).

options.label: Tough conditions (one hand busy, bright light, older users)
options.effect: larger targets and higher contrast by default; reads calmer and more legible [DC-L13-14; S-L13-076, S-L13-038].

questions.ask: Which settings should people be able to change: text size, roomy or compact layout, contrast, or less motion?
questions.example: Show the preview with a mode switcher gaining one toggle per setting.
questions.why: These choices turn on extra modes and larger targets. This follows the inclusive design rule "solve for one, extend to many" [DC-L13-14; S-L13-072].
questions.default: text-size + reduced-motion
questions.default_source: accessibility rule (WCAG 2.2 AA as the floor; text resize and motion preferences are OS settings the system should honor) [DC-L13-14, DC-L10-16].
questions.preview: a mode switcher on the preview screen that gains one toggle per checked setting.

questions.question: Where does your brand sit on these scales?

options.label: Playful
options.effect: saturated brand color on chrome, large radii and pills, springs with overshoot, characters. Serious: neutral or monochrome scheme, small radii, ease-out without bounce, pictograms (M3 Expressive vs Carbon) [S-L06-011, S-L06-083, S-L06-009, S-L06-002].

options.label: Friendly
options.effect: warm neutrals, softer borders, rounded corners, sentence case, contractions. Authoritative: cool greys and deep blues or black, tighter radii, strong rules (Linear 2026 warm gray, Airbnb 2025 curves vs Uber black, IBM grid) [S-L06-067, S-L06-062, S-L06-023, S-L06-003].

options.label: Minimal
options.effect: near-monochrome with one accent, whitespace instead of containers, fewer outlined icons, no hero moments (Notion, Linear). Rich: primary/secondary/tertiary mixing, visible containers, filled or colored icons, 1-2 hero moments (M3 Expressive) [S-L06-092, S-L06-012, S-L06-009].

options.label: Calm
options.effect: shorter, subtle motion (Carbon standard curve), lighter weights, low saturation. Energetic: Carbon expressive curve or springs, heavy weights, high saturation [S-L06-002, S-L06-031, S-L06-083, S-L06-072].

questions.question: One type family, or a pair?

options.label: One family for everything; weights and optical sizes create contrast (Windows, Apple, Fluent, Polaris guidance) [S-L02-022, S-L02-001].
One family with display and text cuts (Google Sans + Google Sans Text; Inter Display + Inter at Linear) [S-L02-006, S-L06-012].
Sans for UI plus a serif (Carbon
options.effect: Plex Sans and Plex Serif) [S-L02-011].

options.label: A separate headline font for brand moments [DC-L02-03].

questions.ask: Use one font family for everything, or pair two fonts?
questions.example: Show a hero and a product panel per pairing.
questions.why: One font family feels calm and unified. A serif or headline font as a partner adds contrast, like in a magazine [DC-L02-03].
questions.default: 1 UI family + 1 mono, with an optional serif or display face for marketing
blocks: Foundations > Typography > Typeface > Families and pairing
questions.preview: a marketing hero and a product panel with each pairing.
questions.use_avoid: add a second face only for a change of job (display vs text, code); avoid near-identical pairs that read as a mistake [DC-L02-03; L15 P49].

questions.question: Which font for code and numbers?

options.label: System mono stack (`ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, ...`
options.effect: Primer, Polaris) [S-L02-017, S-L02-014].

options.label: A brand code font (IBM Plex Mono code-01 12/16; Atlassian Mono) [S-L02-011, S-L02-015].
A style just for key numbers (Fluent Bahnschrift; Atlassian font.metric.large 28/32) [S-L02-008, S-L02-015].

questions.ask: Which font for code and numbers, and should table digits all be the same width?
questions.example: Show a live counter with proportional vs tabular digits.
questions.why: A code font (mono) looks technical. Digits that are all the same width (tabular figures) keep numbers still in tables and live values [DC-L02-05; S-L02-052].
questions.control: single choice + toggle (tabular numbers in tables)
questions.default: system mono stack plus `tabular-nums` on numeric table cells; a metric style only if the product has dashboards
questions.preview: a code block, a table column and a live counter with proportional vs tabular figures.
questions.use_avoid: use tabular figures in tables, clocks and anything that updates; avoid mono for body text [DC-L02-05; S-L02-052].

questions.question: Should the font use in-between weights and reshape letters for each size?

options.label: Static fonts, set weights only (Roboto as applied by M3 components) [S-L02-053].
Variable weight, with in-between weights (Polaris 450/550/650) [S-L02-014].
Variable weight plus optical size tied to font size (SF Pro, Segoe UI Variable 8-36pt, Inter opsz 14-32; Material sets opsz = font size) [S-L02-001, S-L02-022, S-L02-026].

questions.ask: If the font allows, should it use in-between weights and reshape letters for each size?
questions.example: Show 11px to 64px with opsz on and off.
questions.why: Optical sizing makes small text sturdier and large text sleeker. Without it, big headings set in the body version of a font look clunky [DC-L02-04].
questions.default: variable-opsz when the face has it; otherwise separate display tracking and line-height values above about 24px
questions.preview: a size ramp from 11px to 64px with opsz on and off.
questions.use_avoid: use opsz tied to size; avoid setting display sizes in a text cut without tracking adjustments [DC-L02-04, DC-L02-14].

questions.question: What size should body text be?

options.label: 13px (Polaris text-body-md 13/20) [S-L02-014].
14px (Material Body Medium 14/20, Fluent, Carbon productive, Atlassian, Primer) [S-L02-006, S-L02-007, S-L02-011, S-L02-015].
16px (Carbon expressive, Material Body Large 16/24) [S-L02-011, S-L02-005].
17pt (iOS Body) [S-L02-001].
19px (GOV.UK) [DC-L09-04].

questions.ask: What size should body text be?
questions.example: Show a form and a paragraph at 14, 16 and 17.
questions.why: Body text size sets how packed the text feels. 13-14px reads dense, like a "pro tool"; 16-17 reads comfortable and easy [DC-L02-08].
questions.control: single choice per platform (pre-filled from Q-aud-01)
questions.default: web app 14px UI body with 16px for long-form reading; iOS 17pt; Android 14sp Body Medium / 16sp Body Large
questions.default_source: platform convention and card heuristic [DC-L02-08]; L09 shared default row 8.
blocks: Foundations > Typography > Type scale > Base size
questions.preview: a settings form and an article paragraph at each size; the table on the preview shows rows per screen.
questions.use_avoid: use 16px or more where users mostly read paragraphs; use 14px where they mostly operate controls and tables; avoid anything people must read below 12px on web or 11pt on mobile [DC-L02-08, DC-L02-20].

questions.question: Should text sizes change with screen width?

options.label: Fixed everywhere; rely on the OS text-size setting (Carbon productive, Windows, iOS) [S-L02-011, S-L02-022, S-L02-001].
Steps up at set screen widths (Carbon expressive at md, lg, xlg, max) [S-L02-011].
Fluid headline sizes using clamp(), within the 2.5x zoom rule [S-L02-028; DC-L02-19].

questions.ask: Should text sizes change with screen width?
questions.example: Drag the preview width; watch the hero and a card heading.
questions.why: Fixed sizes look steady and app-like. Big headings that grow with the screen fill wide hero banners smoothly [DC-L02-19].
questions.default: fixed body and UI text; fluid or stepped only for display and headline styles on the web
questions.preview: a hero and a card heading as the preview width is dragged.
questions.use_avoid: use fluid type for marketing heroes; avoid fluid styles inside cards, tables or forms [DC-L02-19; S-L02-011].

questions.question: How far must layouts support users' larger-text settings?

options.label: Full scaling, no cap on body text
options.effect: iOS AX1-AX5, Android nonlinear to 200%, web rem [S-L10-011, S-L10-071, S-L10-074].

options.label: Full for content, capped at about 1.5x for fixed parts like tab labels [DC-L10-07].
No scaling support
options.effect: fails platform guidance (Apple asks for at least 200%) [S-L10-012].

questions.ask: When people turn up text size on their device, how far should layouts grow with it?
questions.example: Show a list row at default, 200% and AX5.
questions.why: At the largest text settings, sizes bunch together and layouts must restack. On iOS at AX5, Body is 53pt and Large Title only 60pt [DC-L02-21; S-L02-001].
questions.default: capped-chrome, with every text token in scalable units and no fixed-height text containers
questions.default_source: platform convention and accessibility rule [DC-L10-07, DC-L02-21].
questions.preview: a list row and a tab bar at default, 200% and AX5, restacking live.
questions.use_avoid: use containers that grow with text; avoid truncating at the largest sizes [DC-L02-21, DC-L10-07].

questions.question: Which ratio should generate the size scale?

options.label: 1.125 major second
options.effect: 16, 18, 20, 23, 26, 29 (Material: "Major Second type scale with 14 as its key base size") [S-L02-006].

options.label: 1.2 minor third
1.25 major third
1.333 perfect fourth and above
options.effect: editorial [DC-L02-09].

options.label: Hand-tuned list (11-15 named styles in 12 systems; only Carbon and Ant use a formula) [L09 A1 row 8].

questions.ask: How much bigger should each text size be than the one below it?
questions.example: Show the ladder recomputed; close steps flagged.
questions.why: The ratio decides how many text sizes you can use and how much they differ [DC-L02-09].
questions.control: single choice + manual override per step
questions.default: ratio from Q-dir-03, rounded to even pixels, then hand-adjusted; 1.125-1.2 dense apps, 1.25 mixed, 1.333+ editorial
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L02-09]. Golden ratio is offered only as an optional preset (weak evidence) [BOARD L15 note].
questions.preview: the ladder recomputed live; adjacent steps closer than about 10% are flagged for merging.
questions.use_avoid: use a formula to start and hand-tune the result; avoid keeping two sizes that differ by less than about 10% [DC-L02-10].

questions.question: How many text styles, and how are they named?

options.label: Role x size matrix
options.effect: display, headline, title, body, label x large, medium, small (Material 15 styles) [S-L02-052].

options.label: Named semantic styles (Apple's 11
options.effect: Large Title ... Caption 2; Primer) [S-L02-001, S-L02-017].

options.label: Category plus t-shirt sizes, easy to extend (Atlassian heading.xxlarge ... ) [S-L02-015].

questions.ask: How many text styles, and how should they be named?
questions.example: Show styles used in context: page title, card title, label.
questions.why: Styles named for their job help people pick by purpose and stop one-off sizes. Too many sizes blur what matters most [DC-L02-07, DC-L02-10].
questions.default: role x size matrix plus code, 8-10 sizes and 12-15 styles (13 in the L09 preset)
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L02-07, DC-L02-10]; L09 shared default row 8.
questions.preview: the style list with each style used in context (page title, card title, button label, caption).
questions.use_avoid: name semantic styles by job and primitives by number; avoid more than about 3 type sizes in a single view [DC-L02-07; BOARD L15 note].

questions.question: How should line heights be set?

options.label: Fixed values snapped to 4pt (Material Body Large 16/24; Atlassian; Polaris) [S-L02-005, S-L02-015, S-L02-014].
Fixed values on a 2pt grid (Fluent, Carbon) [S-L02-007, S-L02-011].
Named ratios of the font size (Primer tight 1.25 to loose 1.75) [DC-L02-13].
Plus extra height for taller scripts
options.effect: Medium about +7% (Arabic, Hindi, CJK, Thai), Large +30% (Telugu, Burmese), Extra large +100% (Nastaliq) (Material 3) [S-L02-006].

questions.ask: How should line height, the space between lines, be set for each writing system?
questions.example: Show a paragraph in Latin and Devanagari with clipping flagged.
questions.why: Tight line height makes headings look solid, and 1.4-1.6 keeps paragraphs easy to follow. Line heights set for Latin clip the marks of Indic and Telugu text [DC-L02-13, DC-L02-25].
questions.control: single choice + table of script categories
questions.default: ratio-derived and rounded to 4px: about 1.5 for 12-16px, 1.4 for 18-24px, 1.25 for 28-40px, 1.1-1.15 for 48px+; Medium height for Indic and CJK, Large for Telugu and Burmese; no italics or all caps for non-Latin scripts
questions.preview: a paragraph and a two-line button label in Latin and each chosen script, with clipping flagged.
questions.use_avoid: use smaller ratios as text gets larger; avoid fixed-height components that hold text [DC-L02-13, DC-L02-25].

questions.question: Which font weights, and how is emphasis shown?

options.label: Two weights
options.effect: Regular and Semibold (Windows 11) [S-L02-022].

options.label: Three weights (Carbon 300/400/600; Material 400/500/700; Atlassian Regular/Medium/Bold) [S-L02-012, S-L02-005, S-L02-015].
Four weights (Fluent 400-700; Primer 300-600) [S-L02-008, S-L02-017].
One bolder twin per style (Material Expressive 400 to 500, 500 to 700) [S-L02-005, S-L02-006].
Strong and Stronger variants (Fluent Body 1 400/600/700) [S-L02-007].

questions.ask: Which font weights, and how should important text stand out?
questions.example: Show headings and a selected chip in each weight set.
questions.why: Headings that stand out by size, in regular weight, look elegant and editorial. Headings that stand out by being bold look sturdy and product-like [DC-L02-15].
questions.default: 3 weights (400 body, 500-600 labels, 600-700 headings) and one emphasized weight per style
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L02-15, DC-L02-12]; BOARD L15 note (2 weights per view).
questions.preview: headings and a selected chip in each weight set.
questions.use_avoid: use weight first, color second, italics only inside running text; avoid light (300) below 32px [DC-L02-12, DC-L02-15].

questions.question: Should letter spacing change with size?

options.label: A size-specific table (SF Pro
options.effect: +41/1000 em at 6pt, 0 at 12pt, -26/1000 em at 17pt), applied automatically by the OS [S-L02-001].

options.label: Per-style tracking tokens (Material
options.effect: Display Large -0.2sp, Body Large 0.5sp) [S-L02-005].

options.label: No extra letter spacing beyond the font's defaults [DC-L02-14].

questions.ask: Should letter spacing change with text size, or stay as the font sets it?
questions.example: Show a headline and an all-caps label with tracking on and off.
questions.why: Tighter letter spacing makes headlines look strong and sure. Looser spacing helps small text and all-caps labels [DC-L02-14].
questions.default: 0 at body sizes, +0.02 to +0.05em at 11-12px and all caps, -0.01 to -0.02em from about 32px, in em units
questions.preview: a headline and an all-caps label with tracking on and off.
questions.use_avoid: use em-based tracking so it scales; let optical-size fonts do most of the work; avoid tracking non-Latin scripts [DC-L02-14, DC-L02-25].

questions.question: How should body text be laid out: line length, alignment, cut-off text and spacing?

options.label: 45-75 characters (Bringhurst) or 50-60 (Windows); WCAG 1.4.8 AAA caps at 80, 40 for CJK [S-L02-051, S-L02-022, S-L02-029].
Wrap first, then cut off with an ellipsis (...) and a way to read it all [DC-L02-18].
Paragraph spacing equal to the body size (Atlassian body 12px, body large 16px) [S-L02-015; DC-L02-16].
Trim half-leading so spacing measures from cap height (CSS `text-box
options.effect: trim-both`) [DC-L02-16].

questions.ask: How wide can paragraphs get, and how should long text be cut off?
questions.example: Let them drag a width handle on an article.
questions.why: Very long lines make readers lose their place. Centered or justified text (stretched to both edges) slows reading [DC-L02-17, DC-L02-18].
questions.control: number (max characters per line) + single choice (overflow) + number (paragraph spacing)
questions.default: max prose width about 65-70ch (35-40 characters CJK), start-aligned, wrap then ellipsis, paragraph spacing 1x body size with twice as much space above a heading as below it
questions.preview: an article at the chosen measure with a width handle to drag; lines over the limit highlight.
questions.use_avoid: constrain the container before touching font size when lines exceed about 10-12 words; avoid full justification and centered paragraphs [DC-L02-17, DC-L02-18].

questions.question: Should type sizes differ by platform or viewing distance?

options.label: One semantic scale with platform modes (Spectrum 2
options.effect: 14px desktop, 17px mobile) [S-L02-021].

options.label: Per-platform ramps (Fluent
options.effect: web Body 1 14/20, iOS 17/22, Android 16/24, macOS 13/16) [S-L02-007].

options.label: One scale in each platform's own units (Material) [DC-L02-20].
Sizes by viewing distance, from native defaults (Apple watch 16, phone 17, Mac 13, TV 29 pt) [S-L14-012].

questions.ask: Should text sizes change by device or by how far away people sit?
questions.example: Show one screen at phone, desktop and TV.
questions.why: Phone text about 1.2x the desktop size makes up for touch and distance. TVs and cars need text scaled to how far away people sit [DC-L02-20, DC-L14-04].
questions.show_if: more than one platform or device class
questions.default: one semantic scale with platform modes, mobile about 1.15-1.2x desktop, plus distance modes for TV, car and spatial
blocks: Foundations > Typography > Responsive type > Platform scales
questions.preview: the same screen at phone, desktop and TV with type scaled to a similar visual angle.
questions.use_avoid: keep roles and roughly the visual angle when moving to a farther device; avoid reusing desktop sizes on phones [DC-L14-04, DC-L02-20].

questions.question: What should the base spacing unit be?

options.label: 4 as the grid, 8 as the rhythm
options.effect: named on an 8 base with 2, 4, 6, 12 kept for internals (Material 3, Atlassian, Spectrum) [S-L03-030, S-L03-003, S-L03-044].

options.label: 4 throughout (Fluent 2, Polaris, Primer, Tailwind `--spacing
8 with few sub-steps (Carbon's 8px mini unit) [S-L03-002].
16px rem-based (Bootstrap `$spacer

questions.ask: What base unit should all spacing be built from, like 4 or 8 pixels?
questions.example: Show spacing overlays on a card and form.
questions.why: The base unit sets the smallest step you can see between two spacings. 8 gives chunky, calm steps; 4 gives finer control [DC-L03-01].
questions.default: 4-grid-8-rhythm
questions.default_source: L09 shared default row 2 (4px base, 17 of 22 systems contain the 4-64 ladder) and card heuristic [L09 A1; DC-L03-01].
questions.preview: a card, form and toolbar with spacing overlays; hovering any gap shows its token and value.
questions.use_avoid: use the 2/4/6 sub-steps inside components (icon-to-label, chip padding); avoid them between layout sections [DC-L03-01, DC-L03-04].

questions.question: How should spacing steps grow?

options.label: Fine at the bottom, coarse at the top
Even 4px steps (Tailwind open-ended, Fluent to 56, Primer to 48) [S-L03-015, S-L03-010, S-L03-009].
Doubling
options.effect: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 (Curtis: linear offers "too many choices too close together") [S-L03-039].

questions.ask: How should spacing steps grow: small then big jumps, even steps, or doubling?
questions.example: Show the scale as bars mapped to where each is used.
questions.why: Steps that grow in bigger jumps (hybrid or doubling) make levels of spacing easy to see at a glance. Even steps that sit close together get used in mixed-up ways [DC-L03-02; S-L03-039].
questions.default: hybrid, 12-15 steps
questions.preview: the scale as bars; dragging a step shows where it is used on the component sheet.
questions.use_avoid: keep adjacent steps at least about 25% apart above 8px so the difference is visible; avoid adding steps nobody can tell apart [DC-L03-02].

questions.question: How big must tap and click targets be?

options.label: Web
options.effect: 24px visual minimum, 44px hit area on touch (`pointer: coarse`) [S-L03-035; DC-L03-12].

options.label: iOS 44x44pt (visionOS 60, tvOS 66, macOS 28) [S-L03-033, S-L03-034].
Android 48x48dp, even for small icon buttons [S-L03-029, S-L03-058].
Vehicle 76x76dp (Design for Driving), 64dp parked [S-L14-037, S-L14-032].

questions.ask: How big must tap and click targets be?
questions.example: Show hit areas and the 24px-circle test on a toolbar.
questions.why: Touch target size is a floor for accessibility (WCAG 2.5.8), and it sets how far apart controls sit. A control may look smaller when dense, but its tap area never shrinks [DC-L03-12].
questions.control: single choice (pre-filled from Q-plat-03 and Q-aud-03)
questions.default: keyed to input, not device: the largest input the device supports; gaps of 8px between controls on desktop and 12px on touch; two sub-24px targets never closer than 24px center to center
questions.default_source: platform convention and accessibility rule [DC-L14-03, DC-L03-13, DC-L03-12].
questions.preview: hit areas drawn around every control; the 24px-circle test from WCAG 2.5.8 runs live on a dense toolbar.
questions.use_avoid: decouple hit area from visual size (padding, pseudo-elements); avoid shrinking hit areas in compact mode [DC-L03-12; S-L03-035].

questions.question: Who controls density, and how is it stored?

options.label: Fixed density, no setting (most consumer and marketing systems) [DC-L03-10].
Designers pick a size for each component (Carbon, Fluent, Primer) [S-L03-042, S-L03-046, S-L03-009].
Each person picks a density for the whole app (Salesforce comfy/cozy/compact, Gmail) [S-L03-070].
Stored as its own token mode, apart from screen sizes and color themes. Base values and minimum targets stay the same [DC-L03-11].
Density follows viewing distance and input per device class ("a 65-inch TV is a far-away phone") [DC-L14-13; S-L14-026].

questions.ask: Who decides how packed or roomy the screens are, and how is that choice saved?
questions.example: Toggle a table between modes; targets stay fixed.
questions.why: Letting users pick density can change the layout, not just the padding. In Salesforce's compact mode, labels move beside their fields [DC-L03-10; S-L03-070].
questions.default: consumer: fixed comfortable; enterprise and data: size props plus a user compact mode that shrinks insets, stacks and row heights by one step (about 4px); stored as a semantic mode
questions.preview: a data table toggled between modes; target outlines stay fixed while padding shrinks.
questions.use_avoid: use a compact mode for tables, lists, menus and trees; avoid a type-only density mode that leaves oversized padding [DC-L03-11; S-L03-070].

questions.question: How tall should buttons and inputs be?

options.label: sm 24, md 32, lg 40
options.effect: pointer-first desktop tools (Fluent inputs 24/32/40, 32 default) [S-L03-046].

options.label: sm 32, md 40, lg 48
options.effect: touch-inclusive (Carbon S/M/L; "large 48px is the most common button size in software products") [S-L03-042, S-L03-082].

options.label: XS 32, S 40, M 56, L 96, XL 136dp, round or square, morphing when pressed (M3 Expressive) [S-L08-102].

questions.ask: How tall should buttons and inputs be?
questions.example: Show a toolbar mixing controls at each height.
questions.why: Control height sets the feel: 32px reads as a desktop work tool, 40-48px as touch-friendly, and 56dp+ as expressive [DC-L03-07].
questions.default: touch-32-40-48 for touch-inclusive products, pointer-24-32-40 for desktop tools; one shared height scale for every inline control; derive height as line box plus twice the block padding
questions.preview: a toolbar mixing a button, input, select and segmented control at each size; mismatched heights are flagged.
questions.use_avoid: keep sizes on multiples of 8 and never mix sizes in one group; avoid heights below the target floor without padded hit areas [DC-L08-07, DC-L03-12].

questions.question: How much breathing room between groups versus inside them?

options.label: 1:2, the minimum for clear grouping [DC-L03-24, DC-L15-05].
1:3 to 1:4
options.effect: airy brands, generous margins ("spacious layouts feel calm and open", Material) [S-L03-028].

options.label: Dense sections inside an uncrowded page (Carbon
options.effect: "the whole page should not be crowded") [S-L03-001].

questions.ask: How much more space between groups than inside them?
questions.example: Drag the inner:outer slider on a settings page.
questions.why: Much more space between groups than inside them (8px inside, 32px between) looks clear and premium. Too little difference looks cramped and unclear [DC-L03-24].
questions.default: 1:2, or 1:3-1:4 when Q-dir-02 is spacious
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L03-24]; BOARD L15 note (inner gaps smaller than outer gaps, enforced by construction).
questions.preview: a settings page with the slider live; groups that read as one block are outlined.
questions.use_avoid: use space as the default grouping cue; add borders only where interactivity or scanning needs them [DC-L03-24].

questions.question: How should spacing be grouped by what it is used for?

options.label: Inset, squish inset, stretch inset, stack, inline, grid (EightShapes) [S-L03-039].
Padding, gap, margin; "use padding and gaps before margins" (Material 3) [S-L03-030].
Keep spacing inside parts separate from page spacing (Carbon) [S-L03-001].
Padding shapes
options.effect: square for cards and dialogs, squish (vertical about half of horizontal) for buttons and rows, stretch for inputs [S-L03-039, S-L03-046; DC-L03-05].

questions.ask: How should spacing values be grouped by their job?
questions.example: Show inset shapes on a card, button and input.
questions.why: Naming spacing by its job puts the same padding in every card and the same gap between every field. That repeat reads as rhythm [DC-L03-04; S-L03-028].
questions.default: three families (inset, gap, layout); parents own spacing and children never set outer margins; squish for pill-like controls, stretch for inputs only
questions.preview: a card, button and input with each inset shape overlaid.
questions.use_avoid: use padding and gap on parents; avoid margins on reusable components [DC-L03-04; S-L03-030].

questions.question: Do you need tiny nudges and negative spacing?

options.label: Nudge steps 2, 6, 10 (Fluent; Material nested units) [S-L03-010, S-L03-030].
1px step (Spectrum `spacing-25`, Polaris `space-025`) [S-L03-044, S-L03-005].
Negative steps -2 to -32 (Atlassian, Primer) [S-L03-003, S-L03-009].

questions.ask: Do you need tiny steps for small fixes, and negative spacing for overlaps?
questions.example: Show an icon-label pair and an avatar stack.
questions.why: Tiny steps fix things that look out of line, like icons that seem off-center. Negative spacing lets things overlap, like a stack of avatars [DC-L03-06].
questions.default: 2, 4, 6 (10 only if the icon set needs it), negatives mirroring positives up to 32; 1px reserved for borders, not spacing
questions.preview: an icon-label pair and an avatar stack with and without nudges.
questions.use_avoid: use negatives for deliberate overlaps; avoid using nudges to patch layout bugs [DC-L03-06, inferred].

questions.question: How should spacing above and below text stay even?

options.label: Measure spacing from the text box; spacers snap to the text box (Carbon) [S-L03-002].
A baseline grid (lines all text sits on) for multi-column pages (Fluent) [S-L03-010].
Trim line-height with CSS `text-box` as progressive enhancement [S-L03-077, S-L03-039].

questions.ask: How should we keep spacing above and below text looking even?
questions.example: Measure a button's top and bottom padding, trim on and off.
questions.why: Extra space inside the line height can make padding look uneven, with more at the top than the bottom [DC-L03-25; S-L03-039].
questions.default: snap line heights and spacing to 4px, measure from the text box, `text-box` trim as enhancement; content must survive WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides
questions.preview: a button and card with the top and bottom padding measured, trim on and off.
questions.use_avoid: use a strict baseline grid only for multi-column editorial pages; avoid it for app UI on the web [DC-L03-25].

questions.question: Which icon and avatar sizes should exist?

options.label: Icons 16/20/24/32 (Carbon
options.effect: 16 and 20 pair with 14 and 16px text) [S-L03-062].

options.label: Icon sizes per platform (Spectrum desktop 14-26, mobile 16-30) [S-L03-044].
Icon sized to the button size (Material Expressive 20-40dp for XS-XL) [S-L03-059].

questions.ask: Which icon and avatar sizes should exist?
questions.example: Show icon-label pairs at each text size.
questions.why: Icons sized to the line height sit level with their labels. Bigger icons make the product feel friendlier and more like a consumer app [DC-L03-08].
questions.default: icons 16/20/24/32, avatars 16-64 as Primer; icon size = body line height minus 0-4px
questions.preview: icon-label pairs at each text size, and an avatar row.
questions.use_avoid: keep the icon-to-text ratio fixed ("Don't alter the icon-text size ratio", Carbon) [S-L03-062]; avoid in-between icon sizes that blur the pixel grid [inferred].

questions.question: At which widths should layouts reorganize?

options.label: Material width breakpoints 600 / 840 / 1200 / 1600dp plus height classes 480 / 900 (Android and web) [S-L03-025, S-L03-021].
Tailwind 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1536 (web-only products) [S-L03-016].
Apple size classes, compact or regular for width and height, set by the system [S-L03-032].

questions.ask: Which breakpoints, the screen widths where the layout changes, should you use?
questions.example: Drag the frame across 600, 840 and 1200; show navigation swapping from bar to rail.
questions.why: At each breakpoint the layout changes: panes appear, the menu swaps and columns double [DC-L03-14].
questions.default: material for cross-platform products, tailwind for web-only; web values in rem; design compact first
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L03-14]; BOARD L03 note (Material renamed window size classes to breakpoints, May 2026).
questions.preview: the resizable frame with breakpoint ticks; the layout snaps at each one.
questions.use_avoid: decide layout by window size, never by device type or orientation [DC-L10-10; S-L10-013]; avoid breakpoints that only nudge padding.

questions.question: Should layouts stretch fluidly, switch between fixed designs, or both?

options.label: Responsive
options.effect: one fluid layout (Fluent, Material definitions) [S-L03-010, S-L03-071].

options.label: Adaptive
options.effect: distinct layouts per size (show-and-hide, levitate, reflow) [S-L03-071].

options.label: Stretch inside panes, switch layouts at breakpoints (Apple size classes, Material breakpoints elsewhere) [DC-L03-22, DC-L10-10].

questions.ask: Should the layout stretch to fit, switch to a new layout at set widths, or both?
questions.example: Show a list-detail screen stretching, then becoming two panes at 840dp.
questions.why: Layouts that stretch feel smooth and continuous. Layouts that switch feel native on each device, with different navigation and pane counts [DC-L03-22, DC-L10-10].
questions.default: both, with a list-detail template that becomes two panes at expanded
questions.preview: the resizable frame; pane boundaries highlight when they change.
questions.use_avoid: use adaptive changes for pane count and navigation; avoid device-type checks that break in split view and resizable windows [S-L10-013].

questions.question: How should top-level navigation work at each size?

options.label: Bottom bar on phones (3-5), rail from 600dp, sidebar on desktop (Material; iOS floating tab bar; iPad sidebar-adaptable) [S-L08-083, S-L10-014, S-L10-025].
Sidebar on all but the smallest screens, grouped for 7+ sections (Carbon UI shell, Primer NavList, shadcn Sidebar) [S-L08-009, S-L08-012].
Top navigation (marketing sites) [DC-L08-19].
Hidden in a hamburger or drawer
options.effect: looks clean, hides scope [DC-L13-02].

questions.ask: How many main sections are there, and should the menu sit at the bottom, side or top?
questions.example: Ask for the list of main sections; show them as a bottom bar on phone, rail on tablet, sidebar on desktop.
questions.why: Where the main menu sits is the part of the app's shape people know best: tab bar, rail, sidebar or menu bar [DC-L14-05, DC-L08-19].
questions.default: adaptive-bar-rail-sidebar; primary navigation visible whenever width allows; at most two disclosure levels; no seven-item cap
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L08-19, DC-L13-02, DC-L10-09]; L13 E2 (Miller's 7 does not limit menus).
questions.preview: the person's own destination names in each container across the frame widths.
questions.use_avoid: keep destinations identical across devices and swap only the container; avoid hiding primary navigation on wide layouts [DC-L14-05; S-L13-097].

questions.question: Are your pages mostly for reading, working, or data?

options.label: Reading
options.effect: centered, max about 1280px, text measure 40-80 characters (Primer full pages 1280; Carbon editorial model) [S-L03-008, S-L03-074].

options.label: Working
options.effect: left navigation plus left-aligned content with a max width [DC-L03-16].

options.label: Data
options.effect: fluid, full width (Carbon high-density model) [S-L03-074].

options.label: Material's standard layouts; never more than three panes [S-L03-027, S-L03-026].

questions.ask: Are most pages for reading, for working in, or for scanning data?
questions.example: Show a centered article, a sidebar app page and a full-width dashboard.
questions.why: The page type decides how wide content gets and how panes are laid out. A reading page feels like a document, a work page like a tool, and a data page uses every pixel [DC-L03-16, DC-L03-18].
questions.control: multi-select (page types) + single choice (default pane template)
questions.default: working + list-detail; one pane below 840dp, two from 840dp, three only at 1600dp+
questions.preview: the three page types in the resizable frame.
questions.use_avoid: use fluid width for tables and dashboards; avoid full-width paragraphs [DC-L03-16, DC-L02-17].

questions.question: Which column grid, and how should sections be arranged?

options.label: 4 / 8 / 12 columns (compact / medium / expanded), gutter 16-24, margin 16 then 24 (Material) [S-L03-026].
4 / 8 / 16 columns, 32px gutter with wide/narrow/condensed modes (Carbon) [S-L03-002, S-L03-054].
12 columns everywhere, 1.5rem gutters (Bootstrap) [S-L03-066].
Clear size order or bento tiles for marketing; free layout only for bold pages [DC-L15-07].

questions.ask: Which grid, and should marketing sections use columns, blocks or bento tiles?
questions.example: Show a feature section as columns and as a bento grid.
questions.why: 16 columns allow uneven layouts, like a magazine; 12 split things evenly. Bento layouts of mixed tiles feel curated, with a clear hero [DC-L03-15, DC-L15-07].
questions.default: 4 / 8 / 12 columns; column grid for app surfaces, hierarchical or bento for marketing feature sections; only layout spacing (margins, pane gaps) changes with breakpoint
questions.preview: grid overlay toggle on the frame.
questions.use_avoid: make every grid break nameable ("this hero breaks the grid to signal X"); avoid changing component spacing by breakpoint [DC-L15-07, DC-L03-17].

questions.question: Should components respond to their container or to the window?

options.label: Follow the window width at each breakpoint (media queries) [S-L03-016].
Container queries (Baseline since 2025-08-14; Tailwind v4 ships 13 container sizes) [S-L03-056, S-L03-016].

questions.ask: Should components adapt to the space they sit in (container queries) or to the window width?
questions.example: Show the same card in a sidebar and in the main column.
questions.why: Parts that adapt to the space they sit in look right anywhere, like the same card in a sidebar or the main column [DC-L03-21].
questions.default: page layout by viewport, components by container queries once multi-pane layouts exist
questions.preview: the card dragged between slots.
questions.use_avoid: use container queries for reusable components; avoid viewport queries inside components placed in panes [DC-L03-21].

questions.question: Should a signature shape from your brand appear in the UI?

options.label: Shapes from the logo, used as graphics and as the base for icons (Slack, Dropbox) [S-L06-030, S-L06-024].
Brand shapes, softened for the UI (Atlassian) [S-L06-088].
Curved, soft UI (Airbnb 2025) [S-L06-062].
Mixed shapes that morph, for tension (M3 Expressive, 35 shapes) [S-L06-009].
Strict straight lines and right angles (IBM) [S-L06-003].

questions.ask: Is there a shape in your logo or brand we should echo in the UI?
questions.example: Show Slack's speech-bubble lozenge used as a graphic element.
questions.why: Curves feel friendlier, and sharp angles make people sense more threat. A shape that breaks the pattern draws the eye [DC-L06-09; S-L06-073].
questions.control: single choice (+ upload of the logo for curvature)
questions.default: one radius family derived from the logo's curvature; shape variety only in hero moments
questions.preview: the logo curvature overlaid on the button radius.
questions.use_avoid: use shape variety only in hero moments; avoid shrinking essential actions into small shapes ("smaller shapes can result in essential actions looking less important") [S-L06-009].

questions.question: How soft should corners feel?

options.label: 0-2px
options.effect: official, engineered (GOV.UK, Carbon v11 buttons) [DC-L09-01, DC-L04-02].

options.label: 4-6px
options.effect: businesslike (Fluent 4, Primer and Atlassian 6) [S-L04-007, S-L04-024, S-L04-016].

options.label: 8-12px
options.effect: friendly, modern (Polaris, Paste, Blade, Mantine v9 8px; Airbnb 12px) [DC-L09-01].

options.label: Pill
options.effect: consumer, playful, touch-first (Material 3, Spectrum 2, SLDS Cosmos; iOS 26 capsule controls) [DC-L09-01; S-L04-038].

options.label: Set by size (Spectrum 6-10 by size) or matched to the container's corners (Apple) [DC-L09-01; S-L04-035].

questions.ask: How soft should corners feel: square, slightly rounded, rounded, or pill?
questions.example: Show a button, input, card and dialog at 0, 6, 12px and pill side by side.
questions.why: In L09's (inferred) ranking, corner radius is what differs most in how systems look (divergence 1). Every 2025-2026 update got rounder [DC-L09-01; L09 A2].
questions.control: single choice + radius factor slider (0, 0.75, 1, 1.5, full)
questions.default: 6px controls, 8-12px containers
questions.default_source: L09 shared default row 7 (16 of 23 control defaults at 4-8px, median 6) [L09 A1; DC-L09-01]; a radius factor slider as Radix offers [S-L09-559].
blocks: Foundations > Shape > Radius scale and default
questions.preview: the component sheet morphing as the slider moves; the focus ring follows the radius.
questions.use_avoid: use sharp corners when density and precision are brand values (data, developer tools) and pill when the brand is consumer and touch-first; avoid pill on dense, short controls, which need taller heights [DC-L04-02, DC-L09-01].

questions.question: Which radius steps should exist?

options.label: 3-4 steps + full (Primer 3/6/12/full) [S-L04-024].
6-8 steps + full (Atlassian 2-16/full; Carbon v12 0/2/4/8/16/24/max) [S-L04-016, S-L04-030].
9-11 steps + full (Material 0-48; Fluent 0-40) [S-L04-003, S-L04-006].
No scale; each corner follows its container's corner (Apple) [S-L04-035].

questions.ask: How many corner radius steps should the scale have?
questions.example: Show the steps with a component named under each one.
questions.why: Few radius steps give a tight, even look. More steps let large surfaces get rounder corners [DC-L04-01].
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L04-01]; L09 preset 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, full [L09 A1 row 7].
questions.preview: each step with the components that use it; unused steps are flagged for deletion.
questions.use_avoid: grow radius with component size; delete any step you cannot name a component for [DC-L04-01].

questions.question: Which components get which radius?

options.label: By component type
options.effect: xsmall 2 badges, small 4 tags, medium 6 buttons and inputs, large 8 cards, xlarge 12 modals, full for avatars [S-L04-016, S-L04-018].

options.label: None for nav and tab bars, small 2px for badges, medium, large, circular for people (Fluent 2) [S-L04-007].
Four roles
options.effect: detail 2-4, control 4-8 or full, container 8-12, overlay 12-16+, person full [DC-L04-03].

questions.ask: Should corners get rounder on bigger parts, and should full circles be kept for profile pictures?
questions.example: Show Atlassian's mapping: badge 2, tag 4, button 6, card 8, modal 12, avatar full.
questions.why: Rounder corners on bigger parts keep curves in proportion. Keeping full circles for people gives circles a meaning [DC-L04-03].
questions.default: four-roles; the radius steps up one level each time the element's height roughly doubles
questions.preview: the component sheet with each component's role labeled.
questions.use_avoid: use full radius for people and pills; avoid giving small badges and large dialogs the same radius [DC-L04-03].

questions.question: Plain round corners, or smooth Apple-style corners?

options.label: Circular arc (CSS `border-radius`; every web system) [DC-L04-04].
Continuous curvature
options.effect: SwiftUI `.continuous`, Figma corner smoothing (iOS preset 60%) [S-L04-036, S-L04-055].

options.label: CSS `corner-shape
options.effect: squircle` as progressive enhancement (experimental, not Baseline as of 2026-08-27) [DC-L04-04].

questions.ask: Use standard round corners, or smooth Apple-style squircle corners where they work?
questions.example: Show a 24px card with a circular arc and with 60% corner smoothing, magnified.
questions.why: Smooth (continuous) corners blend into the edges. At the same radius they look softer and more "Apple" [DC-L04-04].
questions.default: circular on the web; continuous on iOS-targeted components
questions.preview: magnified corner comparison.
questions.use_avoid: use continuous corners only where brand parity with iOS matters; avoid relying on `corner-shape` for anything functional [DC-L04-04].

questions.question: How should surfaces separate from each other?

options.label: Shadow ladder
options.effect: tactile, layered (Fluent dual shadows, Polaris 7 levels, Tailwind 7) [DC-L09-02; S-L04-008, S-L04-022].

options.label: Tonal layers
options.effect: flat, calm, color-forward (Carbon layers, Material surface containers, Linear) [DC-L09-02; S-L04-058].

options.label: Borders only
options.effect: dense, technical (GOV.UK, Primer) [DC-L09-02].

options.label: 1px ring plus soft shadow (Radix, Geist, Chakra, Airbnb) [DC-L09-02].
Materials and glass
options.effect: premium, content-first (Apple Liquid Glass, Airbnb) [DC-L09-02; S-L04-032].

questions.ask: How should cards and panels stand out from the page: shadows, color steps, lines, or glass?
questions.example: Show the same card stack with shadow, tonal, border and ring-plus-shadow treatments.
questions.why: Shadows feel real to the touch, color steps feel calm, borders feel technical, and glass feels premium. In L09's (inferred) ranking, this is the second biggest way systems differ in look (divergence 2) [DC-L09-02].
questions.control: single choice (pre-filled from Q-dir-01 and Q-dir-04)
questions.default: in-page containers flat with a border or tinted fill; shadows only for things that float (menus, popovers, dialogs, drag states); in light mode a 1px ring plus soft shadow, in dark mode a lighter surface per level
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L04-10, DC-L08-15]; L09 shared pattern row 12.
questions.preview: the live stack re-rendered per option, light and dark.
questions.use_avoid: use tonal or borders for data-dense tools; avoid shadows on static in-page cards when the same color steps would do [DC-L09-02, DC-L04-10].

questions.question: How many elevation levels, and how do they look in dark mode?

options.label: 4 semantic levels (sunken, default, raised, overlay) with hover and pressed variants (Atlassian) [S-L04-017, S-L04-018].
6 levels (Material 3, Fluent) [S-L04-003, S-L04-006].
7 levels plus special or inset (Polaris, Primer) [S-L04-022, S-L04-024].

questions.ask: How many height levels should surfaces have, from sunken to floating on top?
questions.example: Show sunken, default, raised and overlay surfaces in dark mode with their hex steps.
questions.why: More elevation levels let you show finer order, but they can muddy it. Most products show only three: resting, raised and overlay [DC-L04-11].
questions.default: 4 semantic levels backed by 4-6 shadow primitives; dark mode steps surfaces 3-5% lighter per level (Atlassian #18191A, #1F1F21, #242528, #2B2C2F)
questions.preview: the stack with each level labeled in both modes.
questions.use_avoid: components at the same level never overlap each other; avoid pure-black shadows as the only dark-mode depth cue [DC-L04-11, DC-L04-13].

questions.question: What should shadows look like?

options.label: A main shadow plus a soft all-around one, 2 layers (Fluent) [S-L04-008].
Many realistic layers (Primer floating.medium, 5 layers) [S-L04-024].
Tucked under with negative spread (Polaris `0 8px 16px -4px`) [S-L04-022].
Neutral-tinted shadow color instead of black (Polaris rgba(26,26,26), Atlassian #1E1F21) [S-L04-022, S-L04-018].

questions.ask: What should shadows look like: many soft layers, a two-layer pair, or tucked under?
questions.example: Show a menu with each recipe over a white and a tinted background.
questions.why: One hard shadow looks dated; layered soft shadows look real. Tinted shadows avoid a "dirty grey" look on top of color [DC-L04-12].
questions.default: 2 layers (1px contact shadow plus a soft blur scaled to elevation), neutral-tinted, alpha 8-24% in light mode; in dark mode double the alpha and add a 1px light edge ring on overlays
questions.preview: shadows on the live stack with the alpha slider.
questions.use_avoid: use one light source for every shadow; avoid single hard shadows [DC-L04-12; L15 P62].

questions.question: Should any surfaces be translucent (glass, blur)?

options.label: Opaque surfaces
options.effect: most legible and cheapest [DC-L04-15].

options.label: Glass on navigation and controls only, never on content (Apple Liquid Glass
options.effect: regular for text-heavy parts, clear over media with a 35% dim) [S-L04-032, S-L10-008].

options.label: See-through menus and flyouts only; Mica for the window base (Fluent Acrylic) [S-L04-011, S-L04-012].
Decorative glass effect on cards
options.effect: flagged for legibility (NN/g) [DC-L04-15].

questions.ask: Should menus, bars and pop-ups be see-through glass, or stay solid?
questions.example: Show a toolbar over a photo: solid, regular glass, and clear glass with the 35% dimming layer.
questions.why: Glass looks premium and matches 2025-26 operating systems, and keeps what is behind in view. The cost is lower contrast that shifts with the background [DC-L04-15, DC-L10-12].
questions.default: platform material for native chrome (glass on Apple, Mica on Windows, tonal surfaces on Android); opaque on web with optional blur plus an opaque fallback; content edge-to-edge under the bars with inset-aware components
questions.preview: the toolbar and a sheet over a busy photo with live contrast readouts; the opaque fallback shown beside it.
questions.use_avoid: use glass on the functional layer (bars, controls, sheets) only; avoid glass on reading surfaces and any translucent token without an opaque twin [S-L10-008; DC-L04-16].

questions.question: How thick are borders, and when do dividers appear?

options.label: 1 / 2 / 4px with 1 default, 2 for focus and selection (Primer, Spectrum) [S-L03-009, S-L03-044].
1 / 2 / 3 / 4px (Fluent web) [S-L04-006].
Inset box-shadow borders for states that change width, so layout does not jump (Primer) [S-L04-024].
Dividers
options.effect: space first, then a surface change, then 1px subtle lines (Atlassian, Apple `separator`) [S-L04-017, S-L04-032].

questions.ask: How thick should borders be, and should list items be split by lines, space or background?
questions.example: Show a list separated by lines, by space and by alternating surfaces.
questions.why: 1px borders look light and precise; 2px look bolder and more accessible. More lines make screens feel like a "spreadsheet" [DC-L04-07, DC-L04-08].
questions.control: editable width list + single choice (divider policy)
questions.default: 1 / 2 / 4 with inset-shadow borders for state changes; space first, lines in dense data views
questions.preview: an input switching from default to error without shifting layout.
questions.use_avoid: use lines in dense tables; avoid stacking dividers and card borders on the same edge [DC-L04-08; L15 P64].

questions.question: How dark should modal backdrops be, and how strong are state overlays?

options.label: Black 40% light / 50% dark (Fluent) [S-L04-071].
Blue-black about 46% light / 60% dark (Atlassian `color.blanket`) [S-L04-070].
Tints for hover 0.08, focus 0.10, pressed 0.10, dragged 0.16, disabled 0.38 (Material 3) [S-L04-003].
Stronger tints in dark mode (Atlassian hovered 16%/pressed 32% light, 20%/36% dark) [S-L04-070].

questions.ask: How dark should the shade behind dialogs be, and how strong are hover and press tints?
questions.example: Show a dialog over the page at 30%, 45% and 60% scrim.
questions.why: A darker shade behind a dialog (scrim) pulls focus hard; a lighter one keeps the page in view for sheets that don't block it [DC-L04-18]. Overlay strengths set how every color looks on hover, press and when disabled [DC-L04-17].
questions.default: scrim 40-50% near-black in light, 50-60% in dark, tinted toward the neutral hue; Material overlay numbers, raised in dark mode
questions.preview: a dialog and a bottom sheet over the page with the slider live.
questions.use_avoid: use lighter scrims for non-blocking sheets; avoid scrims so light that the dialog's modality is unclear [DC-L04-18].

questions.question: Should motion feel quick and quiet, or physical and playful?

options.label: Minimal motion (GOV.UK) [DC-L09-06].
Quick, plain curves
options.effect: fast, competent, no bounce (Carbon productive `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.38, 0.9)`) [S-L06-002].

options.label: Plain for most actions, bold for 1-3 key moments per flow (Carbon expressive; Material standard vs expressive schemes) [S-L04-075, DC-L04-19].
Springs throughout
options.effect: alive, physical, interruptible (Material spring tokens, Apple duration + bounce, Airbnb) [DC-L09-06; S-L10-024].

questions.ask: Should motion be quick and barely seen, calm with a few bold moments, or physical and bouncy?
questions.example: Open the same menu and page transition with each setting.
questions.why: Motion sets how lively the product feels (L09 divergence 7). Short, smooth moves feel efficient, bouncy springs feel alive, and no motion feels still but calm [DC-L09-06].
questions.default: two-mode: 7 durations 50-500ms, ease-out to enter, ease-in to exit, springs only for spatial moves in the expressive mode, bounce at or below 0.2
questions.default_source: L09 shared default row 5 (all 16 systems with motion tokens stay in 100-300ms) and card heuristics [DC-L09-06, DC-L04-19]; capped at productive when Q-aud-02 is high-trust.
questions.preview: the live interactions replay on every change, with a slow-motion button.
questions.use_avoid: use expressive motion for page transitions, the primary action and alerts; avoid bounce on everyday controls and in high-trust products [DC-L06-10, DC-L04-19].

questions.question: How should springs be defined and exported?
