options.label: Duration + easing only (Carbon, Fluent, Polaris, Primer) [S-L04-014, S-L04-006].
Two kinds of spring. Moves may overshoot; color and fade effects never do (Material fast/default/slow) [S-L04-060, S-L10-024].
Duration + bounce 0 / 0.15 / 0.3 (Apple) [DC-L09-06].

questions.ask: How should springy motion be set up: time and easing only, spring physics, or Apple's bounce?
questions.example: Show one spring as (dampingRatio 0.8, stiffness) and as Apple (duration, bounce) and a CSS `linear()` curve.
questions.why: Spring animations keep their speed when cut off and come to rest in a natural way. The DTCG format has no spring type, so how you store them matters [DC-L04-22; BOARD L04/L07 note].
questions.default: (dampingRatio, stiffness) plus derived (duration, bounce) for Apple and pre-sampled `linear()` for CSS; critically damped springs for effects
questions.preview: a switch and a sheet driven by the spring, dragged and released mid-flight.
questions.use_avoid: use springs for spatial moves; avoid overshoot on color and opacity [DC-L04-22; S-L10-024].

questions.question: Which durations should exist, and should exits be faster?

options.label: 4 steps
options.effect: micro, short, medium, long (Primer) [S-L04-024].

options.label: 6 steps
options.effect: instant 0, micro 100, short 150-200, medium 250-300, long 400-500, extra 700 [DC-L04-20].

options.label: 16 steps (Material 3) [S-L04-003].
Exits 20-35% shorter than entrances (Atlassian modal 250/200; Primer 300/200) [S-L04-018, S-L04-024].

questions.ask: How many animation lengths should there be, and should things leave faster than they arrive?
questions.example: Show a modal entering at 250ms and exiting at 200ms (Atlassian).
questions.why: Past about 500ms, motion starts to feel slow. Quick exits that people can cut short respect their time [DC-L04-20, DC-L04-24].
questions.default: 6 steps; exits about 70-80% of the entrance; motion is interruptible and never blocks input longer than about 100ms
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L04-20, DC-L04-24]; Apple: "don't make people wait for an animation to complete" [S-L04-033].
questions.preview: a timeline of each transition with its duration; clicking mid-animation shows retargeting.
questions.use_avoid: scale duration with distance travelled; avoid standard transitions over 500ms [DC-L04-20; L13 E1].

questions.question: Which easing curves?

options.label: Standard / enter / exit (Carbon, Primer, Windows) [S-L04-014, S-L04-024, S-L04-013].
Min / mid / max intensity (Fluent) [S-L04-006].
Practical vs bold (Atlassian); productive vs expressive (Carbon) [S-L04-018, S-L04-014].

questions.ask: How should speed-up and slow-down curves be grouped: by job, strength or mood?
questions.example: Plot the four curves and animate a card with each.
questions.why: Easing curves that slow down hard make things feel fast as they arrive. Curves named by job are the easiest to use the same way everywhere [DC-L04-21].
questions.default: standard (0.2, 0, 0, 1), enter (0, 0, 0, 1) or (0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1), exit (0.3, 0, 1, 1), linear only for spinners and progress
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L04-21]; L09 shared default row 5.
questions.preview: the curve editor with a live card.
questions.use_avoid: use linear only for continuous indicators; avoid ease-in for entrances [DC-L04-21].

questions.question: Should shapes morph or use an expressive shape library?

options.label: `radius.full` token only (Atlassian, Polaris, Primer, Fluent, Carbon v12) [S-L04-006, S-L04-018].
Pill reserved for people and status (Atlassian; Carbon v12 moved tags away from pill) [S-L04-016, S-L04-031].
An expressive shape library with morphing (M3 Expressive `MaterialShapes`) [S-L04-005].

questions.ask: Keep one simple full-round shape, or add playful shapes that morph at a few key moments?
questions.example: Show a toggle morphing from round to square when selected (M3 Expressive).
questions.why: Pill shapes look tappable and friendly. Playful shapes (cookies, bursts, clovers) add fun, but work best on avatars and hero moments [DC-L04-06].
questions.show_if: Q-shape-01 is pill or Q-motion-01 is springs
questions.default: full-token; expressive shapes only for playful brands targeting Material, limited to 1-3 signature uses
blocks: Foundations > Shape > Full round and expressive shapes
questions.preview: an avatar, a FAB and a toggle with and without morphing.
questions.use_avoid: use expressive shapes on avatars and hero moments; avoid them on dense controls [DC-L04-06].

questions.question: Which named transitions and stagger should the system ship?

options.label: Fade for in-screen enter and exit (dialogs, menus) [DC-L04-23].
Fade through for unrelated destinations such as tabs [DC-L04-23].
Shared axis x, y or z to show where screens sit (onboarding x, stepper y, parent-child z) [DC-L04-23].
Container transform, where an item grows into a full page [DC-L04-23].
A stagger (small delay between items) of 20-50ms, total at most 500ms [DC-L04-23].

questions.ask: Which of the four standard ways to change screens should we use, and should list items show up one by one?
questions.example: Show a list item expanding into a detail page (container transform) and tabs switching (fade through).
questions.why: Using the same screen transitions every time helps people follow the app. They can feel whether they went deeper or sideways [DC-L04-23].
questions.default: all four plus stagger
questions.preview: each transition playable on the preview.
questions.use_avoid: use OS-owned navigation transitions on native platforms; avoid custom page transitions that fight the back gesture [DC-L10-14].

questions.question: What happens when people ask for reduced motion, and how much motion fits each device?

options.label: Replace movement with fades and color changes (MDN; WCAG's motion rule leaves out color, blur and opacity) [S-L04-067, S-L04-049].
Remove all non-essential motion (WCAG 2.3.3 AAA, technique C39) [DC-L04-25].
Per device
options.effect: system transitions plus brand micro-motion on phone and desktop; subtle focus scale on TV; minimal on watch; none in cars; slow and grounded in headsets [DC-L14-08; S-L14-032].

questions.ask: When someone turns on reduced motion, should things fade gently or stop moving?
questions.example: Toggle reduced motion on the preview; a sliding panel becomes a crossfade.
questions.why: A good reduced motion mode still feels polished, with crossfades instead of jumps. Where people have less attention to spare, motion shrinks, down to none in cars [DC-L04-25, DC-L14-08].
questions.default: replace, built as a token mode; 2.3.3 treated as a requirement although it is AAA; per-device budgets applied
questions.default_source: accessibility rule and card heuristics [DC-L04-25, DC-L14-08].
questions.preview: the reduced-motion toggle on every live interaction.
questions.use_avoid: keep feedback (color, opacity) and remove travel (translate, scale, parallax); avoid removing feedback entirely [DC-L04-25].

questions.question: Do you have UI sounds or a sonic logo?

options.label: Silent by default (most web systems; tvOS plays no alert sounds) [S-L04-074].
Sounds for rare, meaningful events, always behind mute and silent mode [S-L04-074].
Lots of sound (games, spatial computing) [DC-L04-27].

questions.ask: Do you have app sounds or a sonic logo (a short brand sound) you want to use?
questions.example: Play one confirmation sound and show the mute option beside it.
questions.why: Sound confirms actions but annoys people in shared spaces. The builder cannot compose it well [DC-L04-27; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.default: silent on web and productivity apps
questions.preview: the event list with a play button per sound and the mute state.
questions.use_avoid: use sound only for rare, meaningful events that honor silent mode; avoid sounds on web and in shared-space products [DC-L04-27].

hook.accepts: Apple notification sounds as Linear PCM, IMA4, µLaw or aLaw in .aiff, .wav or .caf under 30 seconds; Android decodes Ogg (Vorbis, Opus), WAV, MP3, AAC and FLAC [S-L17-550, S-L17-551, S-L17-552]
hook.if_no: (1) stay silent, the norm for web and productivity apps; (2) use platform system sounds (Android `SoundEffectConstants`, iOS system behavior); (3) commission a sound designer for a sonic logo, noting that repeated identical sounds feel mechanical; no verified open UI-sound library was found [S-L04-074, S-L17-553, S-L17-555].

questions.question: On iOS and Android, who owns screen changes, the back gesture and vibrations?

options.label: System screen changes and back gesture, with small brand springs inside content [DC-L10-14].
One brand motion language everywhere [DC-L10-14].
System haptics only (standard controls already play them) [S-L04-043].
About 6 named vibrations (success, warning, error, selection, toggle, light impact) [S-L04-044, S-L04-047].

questions.ask: On iOS and Android, should screen changes and vibrations follow the system or your brand?
questions.example: Show Android predictive back and an iOS swipe-back on the preview.
questions.why: When the system owns back gestures and transitions, the app feels native; Android's predictive back peeks at the screen behind. Custom vibrations (haptics) feel cheap if you use too many [DC-L10-14, DC-L04-26].
questions.default: os-nav-brand-micro and haptics-system; a semantic map only for products with frequent confirmations
questions.preview: the event list with each haptic's platform mapping.
questions.use_avoid: use haptics sparingly ("less is more"); avoid long "buzzy" vibrations [S-L04-046; DC-L04-26].

hook.accepts: Custom haptics accept Apple AHAP (.ahap JSON, intensity and sharpness 0-1) and Android `VibrationEffect` compositions
hook.if_no: system patterns first (Apple notification, impact, selection; Android `HapticFeedbackConstants`) [S-L17-547, S-L17-548, S-L17-549].

questions.question: Which accessibility settings on the device must the system follow?

options.label: VoiceOver, TalkBack and ARIA labels on every icon-only control [S-L10-075, S-L10-072].
Dynamic Type, Android font scale, browser font size [DC-L10-07].
Increase Contrast and forced colors [S-L10-031].
Reduce Transparency [S-L10-008].
Reduce Motion [DC-L04-25].
Bold Text [DC-L10-16].

questions.ask: Which device settings should the design follow, like screen readers, bigger text or less motion?
questions.example: Show the preview under Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency together.
questions.why: Following these settings changes the look for that person. With high contrast on, borders get thicker; with reduced transparency on, bars turn solid [DC-L10-16].
questions.default: all, with high contrast and reduced transparency as token modes
questions.preview: a settings simulator panel with each toggle applied live.
questions.use_avoid: never convey a boundary or focus state with shadow or translucency alone; avoid app-level switches that override these settings [DC-L10-16].

questions.question: Do you have a custom icon set, or should the system adopt a library?

options.label: The platform's own sets
options.effect: SF Symbols (7,000+, weight-matched to SF, 20+ scripts) and Material Symbols (variable font, 2,500+) [S-L05-006, S-L05-002].

options.label: An open-source set
options.effect: Lucide (ISC), Heroicons (MIT, 316), Phosphor (MIT, 1,248, 6 weights), Tabler (6,220), Fluent System Icons (MIT) [S-L05-029, S-L05-032, S-L05-031, S-L05-033, S-L05-014].

options.label: Your own brand set (IBM, Atlassian 1.5px at 16px, Octicons) [S-L05-017, S-L05-021, S-L05-024].
A ready-made set plus your own icons on its template (Material 24dp keyline template; Apple symbol template) [S-L05-001, S-L05-010].

questions.ask: Do you have your own icons, or should we start from a ready-made set?
questions.example: Show the same toolbar in Lucide, Phosphor, Material Symbols and SF Symbols.
questions.why: Your own icons add character, the platform's icons feel at home, and free open sets stay the same across the app. The builder should not draw icons from scratch [DC-L05-01; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.default: platform-native on native apps, one open-source set on web; platform glyphs for system actions (share, back, close, more, search, settings), brand icons for product concepts
questions.preview: the icon sheet in context; swapping libraries updates every icon.
questions.use_avoid: use one icon family per product; avoid mixing two libraries' strokes in one toolbar [DC-L05-01, inferred].

hook.accepts: one SVG per icon on a 16 or 24px master (outlined strokes, no text), or a Figma icon library; icon fonts are accepted but converted, since fonts blur and flash (GitHub moved Octicons to SVG for this reason) [S-L05-038]
hook.if_no: (1) adopt an open-source set whose stroke and corners match the type (the default); (2) commission a designer only for domain icons the library lacks, drawn on the library's template; (3) use AI icon generators only as sketches, with the caveat that stroke, keylines and optical size rarely match across a set [inferred]. Apple's terms forbid SF Symbols or look-alikes in app icons and logos [S-L05-010].

questions.skip: yes; the default library is applied.

questions.question: Outlined or filled icons, rounded or sharp?

options.label: Outlined
options.effect: light, clean, good in dense UIs (Material, Apple toolbars, Fluent Regular) [S-L05-003, S-L05-010, S-L05-014].

options.label: Filled
options.effect: more emphasis (Apple iOS tab bars and swipe actions) [S-L05-010].

options.label: Two-tone (duotone)
options.effect: decorative [DC-L05-02].

options.label: Corners that match the rest of the app
options.effect: pill UIs with rounded icons, 0-2px UIs with sharp icons [DC-L05-02].

questions.ask: Should icons be outlines or solid shapes, with round or sharp corners?
questions.example: Show a tab bar outlined at rest and filled when selected.
questions.why: Outline icons look lighter and sit well with text; filled icons look bolder and are easier to spot when small. Icons bring the brand's shapes and line weight into the app (Atlassian matched its icon lines to its type) [DC-L05-02, DC-L06-13].
questions.default: outlined at rest, filled plus accent color when selected (two cues that survive color blindness); corners follow Q-shape-01
questions.preview: the tab bar and toolbar with style and corner toggles.
questions.use_avoid: keep hover and pressed feedback on the container, not the glyph; avoid color-only selected states [DC-L05-06].

questions.question: How thick should icon lines be?

options.label: 2px lines on a 24px icon (Material weight 400, Lucide) [S-L05-001, S-L05-029].
1.5px lines on a 24px icon (Heroicons) [S-L05-032].
1.5px lines on a 16px icon (Atlassian, Octicons) [S-L05-021, S-L05-024].
Line weight that changes to match the text (Material wght 100-700; SF Symbols 9 weights) [S-L05-003, S-L05-010].

questions.ask: How thick should the lines in your icons be?
questions.example: Show an icon next to a label at 1.5px and 2px strokes.
questions.why: Thin lines look elegant but get weak below 20px, so icon lines should match the letters beside them. Atlassian went from 2px to 1.5px because 2px felt "too heavy" [DC-L05-03, DC-L06-13].
questions.default: stroke visually equal to body text weight at the paired size: about 1.5px for 14-16px text, 2px at 24px
blocks: Foundations > Iconography > Stroke and corner metrics
questions.preview: icon-label pairs at each text size with the stroke slider.
questions.use_avoid: use heavier strokes on busy or photographic backgrounds; avoid sub-1.5px strokes below 20px [DC-L05-03].

questions.question: Which icon sizes, and what drawing grid?

options.label: 24dp icon, 20dp art area, 2dp padding; opsz 20-48 thins large icons (Material) [S-L05-001, S-L05-003].
16px default, 20/24/32 also, tuned to 14 and 16px text (Carbon; IBM 32px master scaled down) [S-L05-016, S-L05-017].

questions.ask: Which icon sizes do you need, and which drawing grid should they follow?
questions.example: Show a circle and a square icon on the keyline grid.
questions.why: Guide shapes on the grid (keylines) make a round icon and a square icon look the same size. Sizes tuned to whole pixels stay sharp [DC-L05-04, DC-L05-05].
questions.default: 16, 20, 24 (plus 12 and 32 if needed), sized to the adjacent text line height; Material construction unless the master is 16 or 32
questions.preview: the icon sheet at each size, magnified to show pixel alignment.
questions.use_avoid: pixel-align at the smallest shipped size; avoid 12px icons for anything interactive [DC-L05-04, DC-L05-05].

questions.question: When do icons need labels, and what color are they?

options.label: Labels by default (Material navigation, Atlassian, Polaris) [S-L05-003, S-L05-021, S-L05-027].
Icon-only for about a dozen well-known actions (search, close, more, add, delete, edit, share, settings), with a tooltip and screen-reader name [DC-L05-07].
One color, the same as the text (Carbon 4.5:1, Fluent solid) [S-L05-016, S-L05-014].
Status colors on status icons (Polaris tone) [S-L05-027].

questions.ask: When should icons have words next to them, and what color should icons be?
questions.example: Show an icon-only toolbar vs the same toolbar with labels.
questions.why: Icons with words feel calmer and clearer; rows of icons alone feel expert but can confuse. Only a few icons mean the same thing to almost everyone [DC-L05-07, DC-L05-08].
questions.default: labels-default plus universal-only; one neutral icon color aliased to secondary text, semantic colors only on status icons
questions.preview: toolbar variants with a label toggle; hover shows the tooltip.
questions.use_avoid: give every icon-only control an accessible label; avoid decorative multicolor icons in UI chrome [DC-L05-07, DC-L05-08; L10 baked-in rule 9].

questions.question: Do you have an app icon?

options.label: Yes, a file with background and foreground layers [DC-L05-12].
Yes, a flat 1024px image only [DC-L05-12].
No
options.effect: see the Hook line.

questions.ask: Do you have an app icon? If not, I can make a stand-in from your logo, clearly marked.
questions.example: Show the icon in default, dark, clear and tinted looks on an iOS home screen and as an Android themed icon.
questions.why: A designer should make the app icon. On Apple it is layered and lit by Liquid Glass; on Android it is adaptive and themed [DC-L05-12; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.show_if: Q-plat-01 includes ios, android or desktop, or the web app is installable
questions.default: one glyph of 1-3 filled shapes on a solid or gradient background, exported as Apple layers, Android foreground/background/monochrome and PWA icons
questions.preview: a home-screen mock per platform with all appearances.
questions.use_avoid: use simple filled overlapping shapes; avoid photos, fine lines, text and baked-in shadows [DC-L05-12].

hook.accepts: layered SVG or PNG layers at 1024x1024 (watchOS 1088x1088) for Apple's Icon Composer, which applies Liquid Glass and generates default, dark, clear and tinted looks; Android adaptive foreground, background and monochrome layers; PWA maskable 512px [DC-L05-12; S-L05-042]
hook.if_no: (1) the builder generates a placeholder from the logo glyph and labels it "placeholder"; (2) commission a designer, the recommended path for a shipped app; photos, fine lines, text and baked-in effects render poorly under system lighting [DC-L05-12]. SF Symbols may not be used in app icons [S-L05-010].

questions.question: How should icons be named and shipped?

options.label: SVG files as the source, turned into ready code for each framework and app (Octicons, Heroicons) [S-L05-022, S-L05-038].
Icon font or variable font (Material Symbols) [S-L05-002].
Name by shape ("Shield, not security"
options.effect: Fluent; SF Symbols) [S-L05-014, S-L05-012].

options.label: Plus extra names that say what each icon is for, in the code [DC-L05-09].

questions.ask: Should icons ship as SVG files or an icon font, and be named by shape or by job?
questions.example: Show `shield_24_regular.svg` aliased as `action.security`.
questions.why: SVG files and the platform's own symbols stay sharp at every size, while icon fonts blur and flash. Naming icons by what they show lets one icon serve many meanings [DC-L05-10, DC-L05-09].
questions.default: SVG source, files named `<name>_<size>_<style>`, size and color as props; name by shape with a function-alias layer; RTL behavior recorded per icon
questions.preview: the exported icon package tree.
questions.use_avoid: mirror directional icons in RTL; avoid mirroring icons that depict real objects (clocks, checkmarks) [DC-L05-09, inferred].

questions.question: How should the logo appear inside the product?

options.label: Symbol alone at 24-32px in the top bar, full logo on sign-in and marketing [DC-L05-13].
Full logo with its name everywhere [DC-L05-13].
Logo in brand color, neutral or inverse (Atlassian Logo component) [S-L05-044].

questions.ask: Inside the app, should the logo be the symbol alone or the full logo with its name?
questions.example: Show the app bar with the symbol at 24px and the sign-in page with the lockup.
questions.why: A small symbol keeps the app's frame quiet and puts the product first; the full logo with its name feels like marketing. A logo in brand color competes with the main buttons [DC-L05-13].
questions.default: symbol-app-bar with neutral appearance inside dense tools; favicon set from one SVG master
questions.preview: the app bar and sign-in page.
questions.use_avoid: give a logo that acts as a link an accessible name; avoid repeating the logo throughout the UI (Apple) [DC-L05-13; S-L10-009].

questions.question: Does the product use photography, and do you have photos or a photo brief?

options.label: No photography [DC-L05-14].
Documentary
options.effect: "frames from a film" (IBM lifestyle photography) [S-L05-046].

options.label: Portraits that treat every person as equal (IBM "democratic"; Dropbox People) [S-L05-046, S-L05-057].
Still life, product or content imagery [S-L05-046].

questions.ask: Will the product show photos? If so, do you have a library or a photo brief?
questions.example: Show a hero with a documentary-style photo and one with a studio product shot.
questions.why: Photos in natural light with true color feel real and worth trusting; film-like color grading plays on feelings. The builder cannot make photos honestly [DC-L05-14; BRIEF requirement 2].
questions.default: none for tools; for consumer products, a one-paragraph photo brief (subject types, perspective, light, color treatment, casting) before commissioning or buying
questions.preview: image slots in the hero, cards and avatars with the uploaded photos, or labeled placeholders.
questions.use_avoid: use real product and people photos where trust matters; avoid stock that contradicts the brief's casting and light [DC-L05-14].

hook.accepts: JPEG, WebP or AVIF exports and a written brief; masters in RAW or TIFF are kept outside the system
hook.if_no: (1) the builder drafts the photo brief from the personality sliders for you to edit; (2) commission a photographer (best for recognizability); (3) stock against the brief: Unsplash (free commercial, no competing service) or Pexels (no implied endorsement); (4) AI images with ownership and uniqueness caveats per tool, marked as synthetic under EU AI Act Art. 50; NN/g found AI images close to stock but failing on visible artifacts and stereotypes [S-L17-529, S-L17-530, S-L17-531, S-L17-578, S-L17-126]. Neutral placeholders are used until real images arrive.

questions.question: Which image shapes, and can text sit on top of images?

options.label: One shape for each place (16:9 hero, 3:2 card, 1:1 avatar) [DC-L05-15].
Text beside images (IBM avoids overlays on photos) [S-L05-047].
A scrim token (a dim veil) under text on hero images, checked for contrast on the worst spot [S-L05-072].

questions.ask: Which image shapes should you use, and may text sit on top of images?
questions.example: Show a card grid with mixed ratios vs a fixed ratio set, and a hero with and without a scrim.
questions.why: A few image shapes give grids a calm rhythm. Text next to images looks clean and keeps photos true; a dim veil (scrim) under text looks like film but darkens them [DC-L05-15, DC-L05-16].
questions.default: 3-5 ratios, one per slot; text beside images, a scrim token only for heroes
questions.preview: the card grid and hero with live contrast readout.
questions.use_avoid: use art-directed crops per breakpoint for heroes; avoid text over busy image regions without a scrim [DC-L05-15, DC-L05-16].

questions.question: Which avatar shapes should mean what?

options.label: Circle for a person, square for a team or org (Primer, Fluent, Atlassian) [S-L05-066, S-L05-067, S-L05-069].
Plus a distinct shape for AI agents (Primer treats bots and agents as square) [S-L05-069].

questions.ask: What shapes should avatars have for people, teams and AI helpers?
questions.example: Show a comment thread with a person, a team and an AI agent.
questions.why: Round avatars feel personal and square ones feel like a company or group. A shape of its own makes an AI helper easy to spot at once [DC-L05-18].
questions.default: circle-square plus an agent shape if the product mixes human and AI actors; sizes 16-64 on a 4/8 rhythm with initials fallback
questions.preview: the comment thread with fallbacks (initials, placeholder) and presence dots.
questions.use_avoid: keep shape meaning consistent everywhere; avoid using the person circle for bots [DC-L05-18].

questions.question: Do you have illustrations or a mascot, and where should they go?

options.label: None
options.effect: empty states use an icon and text [DC-L05-20, inferred].

options.label: Line style
options.effect: precise, calm, technical (IBM: 4px grid, at most 4 line weights, 15-degree angles) [S-L05-048, S-L05-049].

options.label: Flat
options.effect: bold and energetic (IBM) [S-L05-049].

options.label: Loose, hand-drawn lines (Notion) [S-L06-092].
A mascot in loading, error and empty states (Mailchimp Freddie, Duolingo Duo) [S-L06-028, S-L06-026].
Where drawings go
options.effect: spot illustrations for empty, error, celebration; low-fidelity UI for onboarding; hero and collage only on marketing (Atlassian, Dropbox) [S-L05-050, S-L05-057].

questions.ask: Do you have illustrations or a mascot, or should we pick a drawing style and where it goes?
questions.example: Show an empty state with a neutral spot illustration, a mascot, and icon-plus-text.
questions.why: Characters and hand-drawn art add warmth and let the rest of the app stay plain, but too much makes screens harder to take in. A designer should make the illustrations [DC-L06-12, DC-L05-19, DC-L05-20].
questions.default: one style derived from the icon stroke, corner radius and palette; neutral spots for routine empty states, colorful spots only for first run and celebration; no humor in errors
questions.preview: the empty, error and success states with the uploaded art or the fallback.
questions.use_avoid: use illustration only where it has a job (IBM: "have a job to do"); avoid real screenshots in onboarding illustrations and jokes in error states [S-L05-049, S-L05-050; DC-L06-12].

hook.accepts: SVG (preferred), PNG at 2x, Lottie JSON for animated pieces, plus any illustration guidelines
hook.if_no: (1) ship honest icon-plus-text empty states; (2) commission an illustrator with a brief derived from the icon stroke and palette; (3) open sets under their exact terms: unDraw (free commercial, bans AI training and competing packs), Open Peeps and Humaaans (CC0), Blush (no resale), Storyset (credit required, no logos); (4) AI tools such as Recraft or Firefly, where ownership depends on plan, and style drifts between pieces unless one artist or a strict guide owns it [S-L17-519, S-L17-521, S-L17-522, S-L17-523, S-L17-525; inferred for drift].

questions.question: Do you need a middle size of icon (pictograms) between small icons and drawings?

options.label: UI icons 24, pictograms 64, spot icons 120 (Dropbox) [S-L05-058].
UI icons plus a pictogram library (IBM) [S-L05-049].
UI icons only, with drawings for bigger needs (Atlassian) [S-L05-050].

questions.ask: Do you need pictograms, bigger icons for feature lists and welcome screens?
questions.example: Show a 24px UI icon, a 64px pictogram and a 120px spot icon of the same concept.
questions.why: Pictograms fill the gap between plain small icons and full drawings, so feature grids look richer [DC-L05-11].
questions.default: a pictogram tier only with marketing surfaces, drawn with the UI icon's stroke logic scaled up
questions.preview: a feature grid with each tier.
questions.use_avoid: use pictograms on marketing and onboarding; avoid them inside dense product UI [DC-L05-11].

questions.question: Do you have moving icons, Lottie files, 3D art or your own emoji?

options.label: Built-in icon motion (SF Symbols Appear, Bounce, Pulse, Replace, Draw) [S-L05-010, S-L05-006].
Lottie or moving drawings for welcome screens and celebrations [DC-L05-21].
3D assets [DC-L05-21].
Your own emoji or stickers [DC-L05-21].

questions.ask: Do you have moving icons, Lottie files, 3D art or your own emoji to use?
questions.example: Show an SF Symbols bounce on a saved state and a Lottie celebration on first success.
questions.why: Moving icons confirm an action without taking much room. 3D art and Lottie make a product feel alive but belong on welcome screens and celebrations [DC-L05-21].
questions.default: symbol animation only, to confirm an action or show ongoing status; 3D and Lottie kept for onboarding, celebration and marketing
questions.preview: each asset playing in its slot, with the reduced-motion alternative.
questions.use_avoid: use animated assets for rare moments; avoid looping animation near reading content [DC-L05-21; DC-L04-25].

hook.accepts: Lottie JSON, dotLottie (v2 adds state machines and theming), After Effects via Bodymovin, Rive .riv, glTF/GLB and USDZ for 3D; PNG or SVG for emoji [S-L17-541, S-L17-542, S-L17-543, S-L17-556]
hook.if_no: motion comes from the system's motion tokens only (no signature animation); commission a motion designer for celebration moments; community Lottie assets only under their stated licenses [S-L17-544, S-L17-546].

questions.question: Where may brand shapes and patterns appear?

options.label: None in product (Carbon product UI) [S-L06-001].
Only on special screens
options.effect: marketing, onboarding, empty states, hero moments [DC-L06-11].

options.label: Logo shapes used all over (Slack) [S-L06-030].

questions.ask: Where should brand shapes and patterns show up in the product, if anywhere?
questions.example: Show Slack-style logo shapes on an onboarding card and absent from the product table.
questions.why: Brand shapes and patterns make the product easy to recognize and feel warm. Used too much, they clutter screens and fight the content for attention [DC-L06-11].
questions.default: expressive-only
questions.preview: onboarding and a product screen with the motif on and off.
questions.use_avoid: let branding defer to content in task screens (Apple) [S-L06-008]; avoid devices behind text.

hook.accepts: SVG patterns, gradient definitions and shape SVGs, recorded as brand-expression tokens with allowed surfaces
hook.if_no: commission, or ship none; NN/g and gstack both warn that decoration standing in for content reads as generic [S-L17-004, S-L17-021].

questions.question: Which chart types and chart library?

options.label: Bar, line, area, stacked bar, donut or meter, scatter, plus a KPI big number [DC-L05-22].
Chart advice grouped by the question it answers
options.effect: comparisons, trends, part-to-whole, correlations, connections, geospatial (Carbon) [S-L05-075].

options.label: Style a ready-made chart kit instead of building one [DC-L05-22].

questions.ask: Which kinds of charts do you need, and which chart kit, if any, should draw them?
questions.example: Ask for one real dashboard question ("sales by region this quarter") and show the recommended chart.
questions.why: Fewer kinds of charts make dashboards consistent and easy to learn. Unusual charts look impressive but take longer to read [DC-L05-22].
questions.default: core-6 on a themed existing library; chart chrome mapped to text and border tokens; every chart gets an insight title, direct labels, a text summary and a "view as table" option
blocks: Foundations > Data visualization > Chart types and library
questions.preview: a dashboard with the chosen types in the product's palette.
questions.use_avoid: use bars for comparison and lines for trends; avoid pie charts with more than a few slices and 3D charts [DC-L05-22, inferred].

questions.question: Do you have a voice and tone guide? If not, what 3-4 traits describe how the product talks?

options.label: Upload an existing guide [DC-L06-18].
Plainspoken and genuine, dry humor (Mailchimp) [S-L06-014].
Warm and relaxed, crisp and clear, ready to lend a hand (Microsoft) [S-L06-046].
Bold, optimistic, practical with a wink (Atlassian) [S-L06-060].
Your own traits, set on NN/g's four tone scales, with words to avoid [S-L06-013].

questions.ask: Do you have a voice guide? If not, name 3-4 traits in the form 'X, but not Y'.
questions.example: Show Mailchimp's "plainspoken, genuine" and Atlassian's "Bold, Optimistic, Practical with a wink" beside the same error message.
questions.why: Your voice stays the same everywhere, while tone changes with the moment. The product's words and its look must match [DC-L06-18; S-L06-013].
questions.control: single choice + file upload or text (traits)
questions.default: drafted from the personality sliders: 3-4 traits with "but not", 3 copy examples per trait
questions.preview: the error, empty state and success message rewritten in the chosen voice.
questions.use_avoid: use the traits to decide copy disputes; avoid traits every product could claim ("simple", "friendly") without a "but not" [DC-L06-18; DC-L11-05].

hook.accepts: a PDF, Markdown file or URL of an existing style guide
hook.if_no: (1) the builder drafts traits and examples from the sliders for review; (2) have a content designer review them (22% of teams have none) [S-L11-030]; the draft is labeled as a draft until someone owns it [inferred].

questions.question: How should tone change for errors, success and first use?

options.label: By how the person feels
options.effect: less bold for new or anxious users, a wink for success (Atlassian) [S-L06-060].

options.label: By situation
options.effect: straightforward for serious events, congratulatory for goals (Apple) [S-L06-052].

options.label: An NN/g four-part tone profile for each kind of content [S-L06-013].

questions.ask: How should the tone of the words change for errors, success and first use?
questions.example: Show one error and one success message at three tone settings.
questions.why: Errors need a calm look and plain words, while success can have drawings, motion and a wink. A joke may amuse once but annoys after a dozen times [DC-L06-19; S-L06-060].
questions.default: errors serious, respectful, matter-of-fact; success as warm as the brand allows; clarity beats entertainment
questions.preview: the tone matrix with each cell's example message.
questions.use_avoid: use warmth after trust is earned (success, completion); avoid humor in errors and in high-trust categories [DC-L06-19; S-L06-060].

questions.question: Sentence case or title case?

options.label: Sentence case everywhere (Microsoft, Atlassian, Fluent) [S-L06-047, S-L06-056, S-L06-098].
Title case for headings and main menus, sentence case for buttons (Mailchimp) [S-L06-051].
Chosen for each kind of text, then used the same way (Apple) [S-L06-052].

questions.ask: Capital letter only on the first word (sentence case), or on most words (title case)?
questions.example: Show a nav, heading and button in "Create new project" vs "Create New Project".
questions.why: Title case looks formal and busy; sentence case looks relaxed and translates well [DC-L06-20; S-L06-052].
questions.default: sentence case everywhere; all caps only on 11-12px labels with extra tracking
questions.preview: the product screen's labels re-cased live.
questions.use_avoid: use one rule per element type everywhere; avoid all caps for sentences [DC-L06-20, DC-L02-18].

questions.question: How easy to read should the words be, and how long should labels be?

options.label: 6th-8th grade for general audiences [S-L13-091].
10th-12th grade for specialists [S-L13-091].
Button and menu labels of 2-4 words, verb first, naming the result [S-L13-036].

questions.ask: What school grade should the words suit: 6th-8th for everyone, or 10th-12th for experts?
questions.example: Show one help text at grade 7 and grade 12.
questions.why: Shorter text keeps components small, gets cut off less and reads faster. Even experts prefer plain language [DC-L13-13; S-L13-091].
questions.control: single choice + number (max words per button)
questions.default: 6th-8th for consumer products, 10th-12th for expert tools; button labels 2-4 words, verb first; readability over target is a lint warning
questions.preview: a readability score beside each sample string.
questions.use_avoid: use verbs that name the result ("Save changes"); avoid branded or clever button labels [DC-L13-13, DC-L06-22].

questions.question: Which grammar and punctuation rules?

options.label: Contractions, but not negative ones like 'can't' in serious steps (GOV.UK writes "cannot") [S-L06-048].
"You" for the user, "we" sparingly (Apple avoids "we") [S-L06-052].
No exclamation marks in errors [S-L06-049].
Numerals for counts, "to" for ranges [DC-L06-21].

questions.ask: Which writing rules should the words follow, like 'don't', 'you', 'we' and exclamation marks?
questions.example: Show "We couldn't save your file!" vs "Your file wasn't saved. Try again."
questions.why: Short forms like "you'll", the word "we" and an emoji now and then sound friendlier. Skipping "can't" and exclamation marks sounds more formal and exact [DC-L06-21].
questions.default: all four as listed
questions.preview: sample strings updating per toggle.
questions.use_avoid: keep mechanics identical across products; avoid mixing date and number formats (see Q-voice-06) [DC-L06-21].

questions.question: Which short text rules and word list should each component come with?

options.label: Verb-first buttons, clear links (not "Click here"), kind fix-it errors, empty states with a next step [S-L06-052, S-L06-051].
The same step words everywhere
options.effect: Get started, Continue/Next, Done [S-L06-052].

options.label: A maintained A-Z word list (Mailchimp, Microsoft) [S-L06-014, S-L06-047].
Bias-free rules
options.effect: role nouns, singular they, people's own pronouns (Microsoft; Atlassian inclusive-language page) [S-L06-102, S-L06-054].

questions.ask: Which writing rules and word lists should come with each component?
questions.example: Ask for 5 terms users see often ("workspace" or "project"?) and show them in the nav and an empty state.
questions.why: Buttons that start with a verb are shorter and make clear what matters most. Using the same words each time makes it easy to find your way and know what empty screens mean [DC-L06-22, DC-L06-23].
questions.default: all four; a 20-50 term glossary on day one, linted in copy; locale formats and any regulated copy recorded as fixed patterns
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L06-22, DC-L06-23]; K5.3 and K5.5 [inferred].
questions.preview: each component with its microcopy rule and an example.
questions.use_avoid: use the glossary term everywhere; avoid synonyms for the same object [DC-L06-23].

questions.question: What should your components be built on?

options.label: Bare parts you style yourself (headless)
options.effect: Radix, Base UI (v1 stable Dec 2025), React Aria, Ark UI [S-L08-030, S-L08-026, S-L08-032, S-L08-031].

options.label: Styled parts you copy into your code
options.effect: shadcn/ui on Base UI (its default since July 2026), Radix or React Aria [S-L08-020; BOARD L08 note].

options.label: Web components (Polaris, Fluent UI Web Components v3) [S-L08-022, S-L08-010].
The platform's own controls, styled with your tokens (SwiftUI/UIKit, Compose Material 3) [S-L08-103, S-L08-105].
Adopt a system as-is (Material, Carbon, Fluent, Untitled UI) [S-L11-078; DC-L11-01].

questions.ask: Should your components start from bare parts, a kit you copy in, native controls, or a full system?
questions.example: Show the same dialog built on Base UI with your tokens vs stock Material.
questions.why: Bare parts take their look from your tokens, a copied kit looks like its source until changed, and native controls look like the platform [DC-L08-03]. Take a whole system as it is, and you look like it ("websites made with shadcn/ui famously look the same") [DC-L11-01; S-L11-073].
questions.control: single choice per platform (pre-filled from Q-scope-05, Q-plat-08 and Q-tool-02)
questions.default: React web: shadcn on Base UI or React Aria; multi-framework: Ark UI or web components; mobile: native controls; small teams adapt an accessible base and invest in tokens and docs
questions.preview: the catalog re-rendered per base; a keyboard-test strip shows focus order and ARIA roles inherited.
questions.use_avoid: use accessible primitives so keyboard and ARIA behavior come for free; avoid assuming re-themed colors inherit contrast (they don't) [DC-L11-01].

questions.question: Which components are in version 1?

options.label: The core set (about 25, in 8-10 of the 10 systems we studied)
options.effect: Button, Text field, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider, Tabs, Tooltip, Popover, Dialog, Menu, Progress bar, Spinner, Alert/banner, Badge, Avatar, Card, List, Table, Link, Breadcrumbs, Side navigation, Accordion [DC-L08-01].

options.label: Extended (about 25 more)
options.effect: combobox, multi-select, date picker, file upload, toast, skeleton, empty state, drawer/sheet, pagination and others [DC-L08-01].

options.label: Brand and AI extras
options.effect: Logo, AI label and AI button (see Q-icon-08, Q-ai-01).

questions.ask: Which components should the first version have, and when should more be added?
questions.example: Show the core 25 as a grid; ask which screens of their product need something missing.
questions.why: Teams most often pick a system because it has every part they need (79%), but more parts cost more to keep up [DC-L08-01; S-L11-030].
questions.default: core-25; extended components when two or more products ask for them
questions.preview: the catalog grid with a count and a "used by" tag per component.
questions.use_avoid: use the audit (Q-scope-02) and pilot to pick extras; avoid building components no product has asked for [DC-L08-01, DC-L11-07].

questions.question: Should components use settings, or be built from smaller pieces?

options.label: Only settings, called props (Carbon, Primer, Polaris) [S-L08-064, S-L08-068].
Smaller parts you combine, with asChild/Slot and render props (Base UI, Radix, React Aria) [S-L08-087, S-L08-088, S-L08-089].
Figma
options.effect: variants for state, size and type; booleans for optional icons; text props for labels; instance swap for single icons; slots for repeating or freeform content [S-L07-021, S-L07-022].

questions.ask: Should components be set up with a list of settings, or built from smaller pieces?
questions.example: Show `<Button variant="primary">` vs `<Dialog.Root><Dialog.Title/>...</Dialog.Root>`, and a Figma card with a slot.
questions.why: Settings keep screens alike, while smaller pieces allow richer layouts that vary more. Figma slots let each copy of a component change without breaking its link [DC-L08-04, DC-L07-22].
questions.default: configuration for leaf components, compound parts for containers; the Figma mapping as listed
questions.preview: generated code and the Figma component panel for one component.
questions.use_avoid: use slots for cards, modals and lists so instances keep receiving updates; avoid variant explosions for optional content [DC-L07-22].

questions.question: How should components be grouped and named?

options.label: Atomic design (atoms to pages) [S-L08-054].
Primitives / components / patterns (Atlassian, Radix) [S-L08-011, S-L08-021].
Foundations / components / patterns (Carbon, HIG) [S-L08-009, S-L08-086].
Groups by job
options.effect: action, containment, communication, navigation, selection, text input (M3) [S-L08-008].

questions.ask: How should components be sorted into groups, and what should each group be called?
questions.example: Show "Sheet / Drawer / Side panel" mapped to one name.
questions.why: How you group components decides how easy they are to find and whether names match in Figma and code [DC-L08-02].
questions.default: tokens > primitives > components > patterns > templates, with an alias table
questions.preview: the catalog's sidebar regrouped per option.
questions.use_avoid: use one canonical name with aliases; avoid two components for one job [DC-L08-02].

questions.question: One component set for all devices, or one per device?

options.label: One set whose tokens change by mode (Spectrum desktop/mobile values; Carbon AI presence mode) [S-L03-044, S-L14-058].
Shared basics, with a separate set for each device (Wear Compose Material 3, TV Material) [S-L10-026, S-L14-025].
Use the car's own templates, no custom components [S-L14-010].

questions.ask: Should every device share one set of components, or should some devices get their own?
questions.example: Show a phone list row next to the TV focus-row version.
questions.why: One set keeps the brand the same everywhere and costs less, but can leave phone-shaped components on a watch or TV [DC-L14-02].
questions.show_if: Q-plat-02 marks watch, TV or car as first-class or works
questions.default: one set for phone, tablet, desktop and web with context modes; separate small libraries for watch and TV; templates for car
questions.preview: one component across device classes.
questions.use_avoid: split a library when the input model changes (focus, crown, templates); avoid stretching phone components onto TV [DC-L14-02].

questions.question: How many button styles, and how many main buttons in each area?

options.label: Solid, outline, text [DC-L08-05].
Primary, secondary, tertiary/outline, ghost/text, plus danger (Carbon, Fluent) [S-L08-061, S-L08-066].
5-7 styles, adding tonal, raised, discovery or AI buttons (M3 5; Atlassian 7 incl. Rovo) [S-L08-033, S-L08-063].

questions.ask: How many button styles do you need, and how many main buttons can each area have?
questions.example: Show a form footer with primary, secondary, tertiary and ghost buttons, then the same with two primaries flagged.
questions.why: Three button styles feel calm and strict, while five or six fit busy toolbars. Several filled buttons together make nothing stand out and look like ads [DC-L08-05, DC-L13-18].
questions.control: single choice + toggle (one primary per region)
questions.default: four-danger; at most one high-emphasis action per region, placed after the last field in reading order; a destructive button never takes the primary role
questions.preview: the button sheet in every state, plus a form footer.
questions.use_avoid: use style, not size, to mark the preferred choice (Apple); avoid two primary buttons in one group [S-L08-039; L13 E1].

questions.question: How obvious should clickable things be?

options.label: Strong
options.effect: filled or slightly raised buttons, colored underlined links, bordered inputs, color reserved for interactive elements [S-L15-004].

options.label: Balanced
options.effect: filled primary, outline secondary, link-style tertiary, links underlined on hover [S-L15-038].

options.label: Minimal
options.effect: flat, text-only actions [DC-L15-09].

questions.ask: How clearly should buttons and links show they can be tapped or clicked?
questions.example: Show the same card with a filled button and underlined link vs flat text-only actions.
questions.why: Faint clues look sleek, but people take 22% more time and 25% more eye stops to find what to click (NN/g) [DC-L15-09; S-L15-004].
questions.default: balanced, with strong signifiers forced on primary actions; minimal only when density is low and layouts are conventional
questions.preview: a click-test overlay highlighting everything interactive.
questions.use_avoid: use stronger signifiers as density rises; avoid minimal signifiers in dense layouts [DC-L15-09; S-L15-004].

questions.question: What should the keyboard focus ring look like?

options.label: 2px ring, 2px gap, corners = the part's radius + the gap (Atlassian radius.focus, Primer 2px) [S-L04-016, S-L04-024].
3px ring, 2px gap outside, or -3px inside where an outer ring would be cut off (Material 3) [S-L04-003].
Border drawn inside, for tight grids (Carbon $focus + $focus-inset) [S-L08-062].
Two-tone ring (inner white, outer dark) that is 3:1 on every surface [DC-L08-11].

questions.ask: What should the focus ring look like, the outline that shows where the keyboard is?
questions.example: Tab through a button, input and table row with each ring style.
questions.why: A thicker focus ring with a gap is impossible to miss but louder. A ring drawn inside keeps tight grids neat but can fail contrast on filled controls [DC-L04-09, DC-L08-11].
questions.default: outer-2-2 in a high-contrast brand or neutral color with light and dark values, plus a forced-colors fallback (an outline, not a box-shadow alone)
questions.default_source: card heuristics and accessibility rule [DC-L04-09, DC-L08-11; S-L10-031].
questions.preview: keyboard tab-through of the preview screen with the ring on every stop.
questions.use_avoid: show focus only for keyboard (`:focus-visible`); avoid rings that the element's own fill hides [DC-L08-11, DC-L04-09].

questions.question: Which states get their own styling, per input type?

options.label: A see-through tint on hover and press (Material state layers) [S-L01-005, S-L08-095].
Its own token for each state and variant (Carbon) [S-L08-062].
By how people use each device
options.effect: desktop rest/hover/focus-visible/pressed/selected/disabled; TV focused with scale and elevation; tablet pointer lift [S-L14-013, S-L14-071].

questions.ask: How should states like hover, pressed and disabled get their look, and does it change by device?
questions.example: Show a card's states on desktop vs its focused state on TV.
questions.why: A see-through tint gives any color its states for free; a token for each state lets you tune them to the brand. On TV, focus is large and moving; on desktop, the ring is thin and still [DC-L08-09, DC-L14-06].
questions.default: style all eight states; overlays for hover and press, explicit tokens for selected and error; define states once, render the subset each context can trigger
questions.preview: the state matrix for every component.
questions.use_avoid: make hover content dismissible and persistent (WCAG 1.4.13); avoid hover-only affordances on touch [DC-L14-06].

questions.question: How should selected and active items look?

options.label: A pill shape behind the icon (M3 navigation) [S-L08-083].
A line under it (Primer UnderlineNav) [S-L08-012].
A plain look, not the brand color (Atlassian) [S-L08-085].
Shape changes from round to square (M3 Expressive toggles) [S-L08-034].

questions.ask: How should the app show which tab or item is picked?
questions.example: Show a tab bar with a pill indicator, an underline and a neutral fill.
questions.why: Showing picked items in brand color feels lively. A neutral look keeps brand color meaning "action" and nothing else [DC-L08-14].
questions.default: an indicator plus color, never color alone; brand primary reserved for actions in action-dense products
questions.preview: tabs, nav rail and segmented control selected.
questions.use_avoid: use two cues for selection; avoid selection states that look like primary buttons [DC-L08-14].

questions.question: How should destructive actions look?

options.label: Solid red danger button (Carbon, Primer, shadcn destructive) [S-L08-061, S-L08-064, S-L08-065].
Danger in several button styles (Carbon danger primary/tertiary/ghost) [S-L08-061].
Warning for big changes, danger for the final step you can't undo (Atlassian) [S-L08-063].

questions.ask: How should delete buttons and other risky actions look?
questions.example: Show a table row's delete action and the confirmation dialog.
questions.why: Solid red draws the eye and invites mis-clicks on main screens; subtle red keeps lists calm [DC-L08-06].
questions.default: subtle danger in context, solid danger only in the confirmation step
questions.preview: a list with delete actions and the confirm step.
questions.use_avoid: use undo instead of confirmation for reversible actions (Q-form-05); avoid solid red buttons in dense lists [DC-L08-06].

questions.question: Where do icons go inside buttons?

options.label: Icon before the words, if wanted (M3, 20dp) [S-L08-033].
Label left, icon right (Carbon, 16px icon) [S-L08-061, S-L08-062].
Icon spots on both sides (Atlassian iconBefore/iconAfter; Primer leadingVisual/trailingVisual) [S-L08-063, S-L08-064].

questions.ask: Where should icons go inside buttons: before the words, after, or both?
questions.example: Show "Download" with a leading icon and Carbon-style trailing icon.
questions.why: An icon before the words helps people scan; words left and an icon right give Carbon's editorial look. Buttons with only an icon need labels [DC-L08-08].
questions.default: optional leading icon, sentence-case verb labels
questions.preview: the button sheet with icons.
questions.use_avoid: use trailing icons for direction (next, external); avoid icon-only buttons without an accessible name [DC-L08-08].

questions.question: How should the product show that it is working?

options.label: Nothing under 1 s, a looping sign for 2-10 s, a percent-done bar over 10 s (NN/g) [S-L13-032, S-L13-031].
Skeletons (gray boxes) for page or area loads, spinners for smaller parts (Carbon skeletons only on containers) [S-L13-033, S-L05-071].
Spinner inside the button you pressed, which keeps focus (S2 pending after 1 s; Carbon inline loading) [S-L08-067, S-L08-061].

questions.ask: What should people see while they wait, for short waits and long ones?
questions.example: Simulate a 0.5 s, 3 s and 12 s load on the preview.
questions.why: Skeletons, gray boxes where things will load, make pages feel ordered and faster; spinners feel plain and don't say how long. How long the wait is decides which to use [DC-L13-01, DC-L08-12].
questions.default: acknowledge within 50ms; the NN/g ladder with skeletons for first page load and in-button pending states that stay focusable
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L13-01, DC-L08-12]; BOARD L13 note (timing ladder).
questions.preview: the three simulated waits.
questions.use_avoid: use optimistic UI only when failure is rare and reversible; avoid spinners for waits under a second [DC-L13-01].

questions.question: What style should form fields have, and where do labels go?

options.label: Fields with a border (M3 outlined; Carbon) [S-L08-105, S-L08-106].
Fields with a shaded fill (M3 filled) [S-L08-105].
Label always above, hint under the label [S-L13-066].
Hint text inside the box as the label
options.effect: rejected (memory strain, no way to check entries) [S-L13-066].

options.label: Mark only the rarer of required or optional, "(optional)" or "(required)" [S-L08-106].

questions.ask: Should text boxes have a border or a shaded fill, and where should their labels go?
questions.example: Show one field outlined, filled and underline-only, each filled in and in error.
questions.why: Filled fields feel soft and app-like, while outlined fields feel crisp and form-like. Using hint text inside the box as the only label causes seven known problems [DC-L08-16, DC-L13-05; S-L13-066].
questions.control: single choice (style) + single choice (label) + single choice (marking)
questions.default: outlined, top labels of 1-3 words without colons, hint under the label, the rarer of required/optional marked, `autocomplete` on personal-data fields
questions.preview: the sign-up form in each style, typed into live.
questions.use_avoid: use a visible label on every field; avoid placeholder-only labels (a lint warning) [DC-L13-05; L13 E1].

questions.question: When should forms show errors, and should the submit button ever be disabled?

options.label: On submit, a list of errors at the top that takes focus, "Error:" prefix, notes by each field (GOV.UK) [S-L08-077].
When you leave a field ("reward early, punish late")
options.effect: clear the error on the keystroke that fixes it; validate at complete length for ZIP and phone [S-L13-065, S-L13-100].

options.label: Turn off submit on short forms until all is right, never on long ones (Carbon) [S-L08-106].
Never turn off submit; explain the problem instead (Atlassian) [S-L08-085].

questions.ask: When should a form check answers, and can the submit button ever be turned off?
questions.example: Let them type a bad email and tab away, then submit with an empty field.
questions.why: Errors that show too early feel hostile, and checking on submit keeps forms calm. A disabled button hides why the action can't run [DC-L13-06, DC-L08-17, DC-L08-10].
questions.default: on-blur for format checks, on submit otherwise, summary plus inline for forms over about 5 fields; never-disable, with `aria-disabled` and helper text when an action truly cannot run
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L13-06, DC-L08-17, DC-L08-10]; systems disagree (see Disagreements).
questions.preview: the live form with timing toggles.
questions.use_avoid: use on-blur validation for format checks; avoid flagging a field before the person has finished typing [DC-L13-06].

questions.question: How should error messages be shown and written?

options.label: Error next to the field it is about [DC-L13-07].
Error summary at the top of the form [DC-L13-07].
Section or page banner [DC-L13-07].
A pop-up box that blocks the page [DC-L13-07].
Full error page for catastrophic failures [DC-L13-07].

questions.ask: Where should error messages show up, and how should they be worded?
questions.example: Show a field error, a page banner and a blocking dialog for three severities.
questions.why: An error by its field shows the problem where it is; banners flag system problems; dialogs stop what you are doing. How loud an error looks should match how serious it is [DC-L13-07; S-L13-064].
questions.default: NN/g's 13 error-message guidelines: close to the source, visible without color alone, plain words that say what happened and how to fix it
questions.preview: the three severities on the form.
questions.use_avoid: use a fix-it sentence in every error; avoid blame and jargon codes [DC-L13-07, DC-L06-22].

questions.question: Where should messages like 'Saved' show: in place, a toast, a banner or a pop-up?

options.label: Inline or banner by default; toasts only for low-stakes confirmations with undo, never auto-dismissing toasts that contain actions (Carbon matrix of 4 statuses x 7 types) [S-L08-079; DC-L13-09].
No toasts; banners and dialogs only (Primer) [S-L08-098, S-L08-012].
Toasts and flags used widely (M3 snackbar, Atlassian flags) [S-L08-008, S-L08-011].

questions.ask: Where should messages like 'Saved' appear: in place, in a banner, or in a toast that fades?
questions.example: Save a record and show the confirmation as inline text, a toast and a banner.
questions.why: Toasts keep the layout still but flash by and vanish, while banners stay put and are easy to find. Systems disagree on whether toasts belong at all [DC-L08-18, DC-L13-09].
questions.default: inline-banner; the message goes where the cause is
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L08-18, DC-L13-09]; systems disagree (see Disagreements).
questions.preview: the save action with each channel.
questions.use_avoid: use toasts only for reversible, low-stakes results; avoid a toast as the only record of an error [DC-L13-09].

questions.question: For deletes and other risky steps, offer undo or ask first?

options.label: Undo with trash or soft delete for actions you can reverse (NN/g calls undo superior; Shneiderman rule 6) [S-L13-067, S-L13-037].
An 'Are you sure?' box with clear verb buttons, and Cancel as the safe choice [S-L13-067; DC-L13-08].
Undo when it can be undone, ask first when it can't or costs a lot [DC-L13-08].

questions.ask: When people delete something, should they get an undo button, an 'Are you sure?' step, or both?
questions.example: Delete a list item: show the undo toast, then an irreversible delete with a "Delete file / Keep file" dialog.
questions.why: Undo keeps work fast and calm. Asking "Are you sure?" too often feels like red tape, and people stop reading it [DC-L13-08; S-L13-067].
questions.default: both
questions.preview: the list delete flow per option.
questions.use_avoid: use verb labels on confirmations; avoid "Are you sure?" dialogs for reversible actions [DC-L13-08].

questions.question: When should the product use a dialog, a sheet or a popover?

options.label: Block the page only if it clearly helps; panels and pop-ups for small tasks; full screen for big flows (HIG) [S-L08-086].
Panels that slide in from the bottom or side (M3, Fluent, Atlassian) [S-L08-008, S-L08-010, S-L08-011].
Floating "levitate" panes for focused tasks (M3) [S-L08-096].

questions.ask: Which tasks should open in a box in the middle, a panel that slides in, or a small pop-up?
questions.example: Edit a record in a dialog vs a side sheet on the preview.
questions.why: A centered dialog stops people in their tracks. A side sheet keeps the page in view, and a popover feels light [DC-L08-20].
questions.default: dialog for short decisions, side sheet for editing with context, bottom sheet on phones; each platform's button order
questions.preview: the same edit task in each overlay.
questions.use_avoid: use a dismiss path on every dialog (missing one is a lint error); avoid stacking modals [DC-L08-20; L13 E1].

questions.question: How should long lists load: pages, "load more", or infinite scroll?

options.label: Page numbers (Carbon, Atlassian, Primer, shadcn) [DC-L08-21].
Load more [S-L08-073].
Infinite scroll, for feeds of same-kind items [S-L08-073].

questions.ask: How should long lists load: in pages, with a 'Load more' button, or by scrolling on and on?
questions.example: Show a table with pagination and a feed with infinite scroll.
questions.why: Numbered pages help people find their place again. Infinite scroll feels endless, and a "Load more" button keeps the footer in reach [DC-L08-21].
questions.default: pagination for tables and goal-directed search, load more for result lists, infinite scroll only for feeds
questions.preview: each collection type on the preview.
questions.use_avoid: use pagination where people need to return to a position; avoid infinite scroll above a footer people need [DC-L08-21].

questions.question: How much should be visible up front, and how much behind "more"?

options.label: Show everything at once [DC-L13-03].
Main options first, extras behind a clearly named button, two levels at most [S-L13-063].
One step at a time (a wizard), only when steps stand alone [S-L13-063].
Show extras on hover or when something is picked [DC-L13-03].

questions.ask: Should people see every option at once, or the main ones first with the rest tucked away?
questions.example: Show a settings page with an "Advanced" section collapsed and expanded.
questions.why: Keeping extras one step away (progressive disclosure) makes screens calm and short. Showing it all at once feels strong, but busy [DC-L13-03].
questions.default: progressive
questions.preview: the settings page per option.
questions.use_avoid: use steppers that show position and total; avoid more than two disclosure levels (a lint warning) [DC-L13-03; L13 E1].

questions.question: How should empty states and first-time use work?

options.label: Empty states for first use, user-cleared, no results, no permission or error (Primer Blankslate, Spectrum IllustratedMessage, shadcn Empty) [DC-L13-10; S-L08-012, S-L08-015, S-L08-018].
No onboarding
options.effect: a self-evident UI (NN/g's first recommendation) [S-L13-070].

options.label: Tips and empty-screen hints right when people need them [S-L13-070].
A guided tour, only for truly new and complex screens [S-L13-070].

questions.ask: What should an empty screen show, and how should first-time users learn the product?
questions.example: Show a first-use empty project list, a no-results search and a tour with a skip button.
questions.why: A well-made empty state teaches and invites people in. A blank area looks broken, and forced tours slow people down at the start [DC-L13-10, DC-L13-11].
questions.default: every collection gets empty variants that state status, help learning and give a direct action; contextual onboarding; everything skippable
questions.preview: each empty-state kind with the illustration choice from Q-img-04.
questions.use_avoid: use an empty state on every collection (missing one is a lint warning); avoid tours without a skip control [DC-L13-10, DC-L13-11; L13 E1].

questions.question: Which deceptive patterns should the builder block?

options.label: No policy [DC-L13-15].
A written ban on the 16 tricks at deceptive.design, like sneaking and fake urgency [S-L13-071].
Written down, and blocked where a tool can spot it
options.effect: pre-checked consent or marketing boxes and unequal accept/reject emphasis are lint errors; re-prompting after dismissal is flagged [S-L13-071, S-L13-108].

questions.ask: How firmly should we stop design tricks, like boxes ticked for you or a louder 'Yes' button?
questions.example: Show a consent dialog with equal buttons vs a "confirmshaming" one, flagged.
questions.why: Fair defaults make 'Accept' and 'Decline' look equal and leave opt-in boxes unticked. They also word 'Decline' without guilt [DC-L13-15].
questions.default: enforced
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L13-15]; L13 E1 lint errors.
questions.preview: a consent dialog and a cancellation flow checked live.
questions.use_avoid: use equal emphasis for accept and reject; avoid nagging and fake urgency (the Zeigarnik effect does not justify nags) [DC-L13-15; L13 E2].

questions.question: What should small glance views show, like widgets, tiles and watch complications?

options.label: One fact per complication, one or two per tile, alerts when urgent, all in the app (Google) [S-L14-015].
Complications, Smart Stack, Live Activities, CarPlay widgets [S-L14-001, S-L14-047].

questions.ask: What one number or status should people see without opening the app?
questions.example: Ask for the one metric; show it as a watch complication and a home-screen widget.
questions.why: Glance views should look like data, not app screens: big numbers, one metric, a status color and almost no frame around them [DC-L14-07].
questions.show_if: Q-plat-02 marks watch or car first-class, or the product ships widgets
questions.default: design the complication or tile first, then the app; one number or status per glance
questions.preview: the metric on each glance surface.
questions.use_avoid: use tiles that are "immediate, predictable, relevant"; avoid shrinking app screens into widgets [S-L14-020; DC-L14-07].

questions.question: Does the product have AI features, and how should AI content be marked?

options.label: No AI features.
An AI tag and an AI button (Carbon AI label; S2 genai; Atlassian Rovo) [S-L08-009, S-L08-067, S-L08-063].
An AI mode that normal parts can switch on
options.effect: label, explainability popover, glow tokens, revert (Carbon) [S-L14-058].

options.label: Chat components for products people talk to (shadcn Message, Bubble; Carbon AI chat) [S-L08-018, S-L14-058].
Voice-only turns
options.effect: one breath, 2-5 options (Alexa) [S-L14-065].

questions.ask: Does your product use AI, and if so, how should people spot and fix its work?
questions.example: Show an AI-generated summary with a label, citations, and Edit / Undo / Retry.
questions.why: Clear AI labels and sources shown apart make AI output read as "assistive, check me". A separate AI accent color can compete with your main action color [DC-L13-16, DC-L08-22].
questions.default: label-button as an optional module, chat only for conversational products; label AI content, place citations next to claims, express uncertainty in high-stakes contexts, and pair every generated output with Edit, Undo and Retry
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L08-22, DC-L13-16, DC-L14-12; S-L13-089, S-L14-011].
questions.preview: AI output in a table cell, a side panel and a chat thread.
questions.use_avoid: use AI styling only on AI-generated content (Carbon warns against decoration); avoid human-sounding anthropomorphic framing and reasoning traces presented as explanations [DC-L14-12, DC-L13-16].

questions.question: How many token layers should sit between raw values and components?

options.label: One layer
options.effect: palette and scales used directly (Tailwind); theming means find-and-replace [DC-L07-01].

options.label: Two layers, raw then role, plus component tokens when needed (Atlassian, Polaris; Fluent global + alias) [S-L07-107, S-L07-125, S-L01-033].
Three layers for every part, raw, role, then part (Material 3; Primer base, functional, component) [S-L07-102, S-L01-027].

questions.ask: Should buttons and cards use raw colors and sizes, or go through layers of named values?
questions.example: Show `blue.600` -> `color.bg.accent` -> `button.primary.bg`, and which layer a rebrand edits.
questions.why: A layer of role names (semantic tokens) lets you change the look, like a rebrand or a new mode, without touching components. 24 of the 25 systems we studied have one [DC-L07-01; L09 A1 row 1].
questions.default: two-plus: primitives private, semantics public, component tokens only for components a brand must restyle or values shared by 3+ components; typography as primitives, semantic composites `text.{role}.{size}` and optional component aliases
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L07-01, DC-L07-02, DC-L01-26, DC-L02-27]; L09 counts this as its 3-tier default with the component tier optional.
questions.preview: the token chain inspector on the preview.
questions.use_avoid: use semantic tokens in every component; avoid components referencing a raw hex or px (L09: 24 of 25 systems forbid it) [L09 A1 row 1].

questions.question: Which units should the source use?

options.label: px in source, rem on the web (DTCG allows px and rem only; Figma imports px) [S-L07-002, S-L07-011, S-L03-037].
Plain numbers in steps of 4, output 1:1 as pt, dp, epx or px; rem for web font sizes (Fluent's ramp) [S-L10-039].
rem in the source, turned into dp, sp or CGFloat by the build [DC-L10-08].

questions.ask: Should stored sizes be pixels, plain numbers, or rem (the web unit that grows with the browser's text size)?
questions.example: Show `16` becoming `1rem`, `16pt`, `16dp` and `16px`.
questions.why: px maps cleanly to pt, dp and Figma. rem follows browser zoom, and plain numbers carry over 1:1 to every platform [DC-L07-11, DC-L10-08].
questions.control: single choice + toggle (spacing scales with text)
questions.default: px-to-rem (equivalently unitless numbers), rem for web type and breakpoints; "spacing scales with text size" is an explicit toggle, off by default; line height unitless
questions.preview: one value converted per platform.
questions.use_avoid: question any value not divisible by 4 (except 2, 6, 10 for icon nudges); avoid sp or rem for spacing that must not scale with text on Android [DC-L10-08; L10 baked-in rule 4].

questions.question: Which file format and build pipeline should produce platform code?

options.label: DTCG 2025.10 + Resolver, one file per tier and mode (stable since 28 Oct 2025) [S-L07-002, S-L07-004].
Terrazzo 2.x
options.effect: full DTCG including resolvers, web-strong [S-L07-179].

options.label: Style Dictionary v5
options.effect: widest native coverage (Compose, Android XML, Swift, Flutter), no resolver support, so one build per combination [S-L07-151, S-L07-162, S-L10-056].

options.label: Tokens Studio + sd-transforms, when designers author in the plugin [DC-L07-25].
Web
options.effect: CSS custom properties for semantics, media queries for preferences, container queries for components [S-L10-052, S-L10-031].

questions.ask: Which file format and build tool should turn your tokens into code for each platform?
questions.example: Show the output tree: CSS variables, Tailwind theme, Swift, Compose.
questions.why: The build tool decides if tokens reach each codebase in the style that code already uses [DC-L07-25, DC-L10-22].
questions.default: dtcg-resolver as the canonical export; Terrazzo for web-only teams, Style Dictionary v5 when native outputs are needed; web-delivery on the web
questions.preview: the generated file tree with one file open.
questions.use_avoid: use one canonical export and generate everything else from it; avoid hand-edited platform files [DC-L07-25].

questions.question: How should tokens be named?

options.label: Names in a fixed order, like ds.color.bg.accent.hover, for roles and parts [DC-L07-04].
Raw color names
options.effect: hue + numeric step (50-950 or bounded 0-100); descriptive names only for brand colors [DC-L07-03].

options.label: Space steps named by percent of base (space.200 = 16px; Atlassian, Material), and role names [S-L03-003, S-L03-030].
A 2-4 letter prefix in code only (--ds-, --cds-, --md-); no theme or brand in names [S-L07-036, S-L07-108].
Lowercase JSON segments; kebab for CSS, camel for JS/Swift/Kotlin, snake for Android XML [S-L07-158].

questions.ask: What naming rules should tokens follow, so people and AI tools read them the same way?
questions.example: Show `ds.color.bg.accent.hover`, `space.200`, and `--ds-color-bg-accent-hover` in CSS.
questions.why: Token names are the shared words for people and AI agents. Use only as many name parts as it takes to tell tokens apart [DC-L07-04; S-L07-036].
questions.default: all five as listed
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L07-03, DC-L07-04, DC-L07-05, DC-L07-06, DC-L03-03].
questions.preview: a name linter that shows each token's name in JSON, CSS, Swift and Kotlin.
questions.use_avoid: use role names at the semantic tier; avoid `padding` or `margin` in primitive names and ordinal scales that look proportional but aren't [DC-L03-03].

questions.question: Which kinds of values should become tokens?

options.label: Color, type, space [DC-L07-07].
Plus corners, borders, shadows, opacity and motion [DC-L07-07].
Plus layer order (z-index), breakpoints, icon sizes, touch targets and chart colors [DC-L07-07; S-L07-036].

questions.ask: Which kinds of values should get a token, from the basics up to almost all of them?
questions.example: Show the coverage list with counts per category.
questions.why: A value without a token drifts over time, and lint rules can't check it and themes can't change it [DC-L07-07].
questions.default: extended; one-off illustration values stay untokenized
questions.preview: a coverage bar per category.
questions.use_avoid: use tokens for anything a lint rule should check; avoid tokenizing one-off art values [DC-L07-07].

questions.question: How should bundled values like text styles, shadows and motion be stored?

options.label: Typography
options.effect: atomic primitives + semantic `typography` composites; Figma text styles with fields bound to variables (bind if more than one brand or platform) [S-L07-013, S-L07-019, S-L02-036].

options.label: Shadows and borders
options.effect: DTCG `shadow` and `border` composites; Figma effect styles with bound color and offsets [S-L07-002, S-L07-020].

options.label: Motion
options.effect: DTCG `duration`, `cubicBezier`, `transition`; Figma timing and easing variables with a reduced-motion mode; springs as `{dampingRatio, stiffness}` in `$extensions` with a bezier fallback [S-L07-033, S-L04-052].

questions.ask: How should styles made of several values, like a text style or a shadow, be stored?
questions.example: Show a `typography` composite in JSON and the Figma text style bound to its variables.
questions.why: Bundled tokens keep a style whole in code, and Figma styles bound to variables switch with each mode. DTCG has no type for springs [DC-L07-12, DC-L07-13, DC-L07-14, DC-L04-28].
questions.default: all three as listed
questions.default_source: card heuristics [DC-L07-12, DC-L07-13, DC-L07-14, DC-L04-28, DC-L02-28].
questions.preview: JSON and Figma views of one token of each type.
questions.use_avoid: use variables for single values that change by mode and styles for bundles; avoid hard-coded style values [DC-L07-21].

questions.question: How should themes and modes combine without too many versions to test?

options.label: Every mix in one flat list (the DTCG resolver example
options.effect: light, lightHighContrast, dark, darkHighContrast) [S-L07-004].

options.label: Separate settings that never change the same tokens [DC-L07-17].
Figma collections
options.effect: Primitives (hidden) + Semantic color + Semantic dimension (density or breakpoint) + Motion with a reduced mode [DC-L07-18].

options.label: A Breakpoint collection (3 modes) for layout, and grid auto layout for parts with columns [DC-L07-28; S-L07-024].

questions.ask: How should dark mode, contrast and density mix without too many versions to test?
questions.example: Show 2 schemes x 2 contrasts x 2 densities as additive collections instead of 8 flattened modes.
questions.why: Each extra setting, like dark mode or density, multiplies what you must test. If two settings change the same token, they should be one setting [DC-L07-17].
questions.default: orthogonal with at most 3 axes plus collections and a breakpoint collection
questions.preview: the combination count and the Figma mode budget from Q-tool-03.
questions.use_avoid: use additive collections to stay within the plan's mode limit; avoid putting brand and scheme in one flattened axis [DC-L07-18, DC-L07-27].

questions.question: How should the Figma library be kept clean?

options.label: Hide raw values, and offer each variable only where its name fits [S-L07-018, S-L07-025].
Make Web, Android and iOS code names from the build's name rules [S-L07-018].
Variables for values, styles for bundles [S-L07-019].
Run Check designs before "Ready for dev" and review library analytics quarterly (Org/Enterprise; the builder lints on Professional) [S-L07-025, S-L07-029].

questions.ask: How should the Figma library stay tidy, so designers pick the right values?
questions.example: Show a text-color variable offered only in text fill pickers.
questions.why: Hiding raw values and limiting where each variable shows up keeps designers on semantic tokens. Generated code names keep the names the same in Figma and in code [DC-L07-19, DC-L07-20].
questions.default: all four
questions.preview: the Figma variable panel as a designer would see it.
questions.use_avoid: use scopes so a spacing token cannot be picked for a color; avoid "show in all" scopes [DC-L07-19].

questions.question: How should tokens be described and retired?

options.label: A short note ($description) on each semantic token [S-L07-002].
`$deprecated
options.effect: true` or "Use X instead", one release before removal [S-L07-002].

options.label: Check library analytics before you remove it (Org/Enterprise) [S-L07-029].
