questions.ask: How should each token explain its use, and how should old tokens be phased out?
questions.example: Show `$deprecated: "Use color.bg.accent instead"` in JSON and the warning in Figma.
questions.why: A short description tells people and AI agents what each token is for. Marking a token as old before deleting it protects the teams that use it [DC-L07-23].
questions.default: all three
questions.preview: a token's detail card with description and status.
questions.use_avoid: use descriptions written for agents as well as people; avoid deleting tokens without a replacement [DC-L07-23].

questions.question: Which inputs should re-skin the theme, and what may other brands or clients customize?

options.label: Three generator inputs
options.effect: brand color, neutral base or temperature, contrast (Linear) [S-L06-012; DC-L06-06].

options.label: One source color plus a scheme variant and contrast level (Material) [S-L06-082, S-L06-083].
One brand color in code (Blade `createTheme({brandColor})`) [S-L06-094].
An admin page, "clicks, not code", for colors, logos, images and chosen accents (Salesforce SLDS 2) [S-L06-068].
A theme builder for your users (Linear base, accent, contrast) [S-L06-012].
Overrides people edit in the CMS [S-L06-053].

questions.ask: What should set the theme's look, and what may clients or other brands change?
questions.example: Show a client admin panel with a color picker, logo upload and a live contrast check.
questions.why: Fewer inputs give themes that are more consistent and always accessible, but with less nuance. Linear swapped 98 per-theme variables for 3 inputs [DC-L06-06; S-L06-012]. When other brands restyle a product, they almost always change color and type [DC-L06-17; S-L06-053].
questions.default: three generator inputs; clients may change brand color and logo, font and radius only with previews and validation
questions.preview: the client panel re-skinning the preview with contrast re-checked.
questions.use_avoid: use generated on-colors so client colors keep contrast; avoid exposing raw token editing to clients [DC-L06-17, DC-L06-16].

questions.question: How strict should the system be: can product teams override or extend it?

options.label: Strict
options.effect: comprehensive docs, design and code fully synced, little deviation [S-L11-018, S-L11-019].

options.label: Loose
options.effect: a framework with room to experiment [S-L11-019].

options.label: A strict core, plus team-owned add-ons, the "expanded universe" (Dan Mall) [S-L11-014].

questions.ask: How strict should the system be, and can product teams change it or add their own parts?
questions.example: Show which layers are locked and which are open under each option.
questions.why: A strict system stays consistent but feels rigid, and a loose one allows experiments but drifts. A strict core with loose edges is the practical middle [DC-L11-03].
questions.default: strict core (tokens, primitives, accessibility behavior), loose edges (patterns, marketing)
questions.preview: a layer diagram with lock icons per layer.
questions.use_avoid: use a snowflake path for one-off needs; avoid forcing every product-specific component into the core [DC-L11-03, DC-L11-12].

questions.question: In what order will you build, pilot and roll out?

options.label: Foundations first
options.effect: spacing, color, type, elevation, icons, then components (Figma course order) [S-L11-009].

options.label: Start with a pilot product
options.effect: extract components from a real product, apply to the next [S-L11-014].

options.label: Pick the pilot by 8 tests, like shared parts, a champion, a 3-4 week scope and few ties to old code [S-L11-105].
Roll out step by step, worst problems first; all at once only with a rebrand [S-L11-105].

questions.ask: In what order will you build the system, try it in one product, and roll it out?
questions.example: Show Dan Mall's 8-criteria pilot scorecard filled for two candidate products.
questions.why: Foundations first is tidy but abstract. A pilot product keeps components real. Launching all at once draws attention but risks bias toward that pilot [DC-L11-06, DC-L11-07, DC-L11-08].
questions.default: minimal foundations first, then pilot-driven components, incremental rollout
questions.preview: a timeline of the plan.
questions.use_avoid: use a second pilot from a different product family to reduce bias; avoid building components no pilot needs [DC-L11-07].

questions.question: Who can contribute, and how are decisions made and recorded?

options.label: Closed or narrow
options.effect: fixes and small enhancements only (Atlassian) [S-L11-024].

options.label: Open, with checks
options.effect: proposals must be useful and unique; publication must be usable, consistent, versatile (GOV.UK) [S-L11-021].

options.label: A fast lane for fixes, icons and docs; a proposal (RFC) lane for new components [S-L11-020, S-L11-021].
Brad Frost's 10-step flow, with a path for one-off needs [S-L11-003].
Decision records (ADRs) from day one, made from your answers here [S-L11-095; inferred].

questions.ask: Who can add to the system, and how will decisions be made and written down?
questions.example: Show a decision record generated from one of this session's answers.
questions.why: Only 36% of teams are happy with how people add to their system. Decision records explain why things are the way they are [DC-L11-11, DC-L11-12; S-L11-030].
questions.default: two-lanes, frost-flow and adrs
questions.preview: the generated decision log.
questions.use_avoid: record why an option was chosen and what it beat; avoid undocumented overrides [DC-L11-12].

questions.question: How should each part get a status, a version number, and a way to retire?

options.label: Experimental, then Ready, then Deprecated (Primer cut five to three) [S-L11-025, S-L11-026].
One SemVer for the whole library while small; one per package on many platforms [S-L11-106, S-L11-028].
A version number for each component (Atlassian, Paste) [S-L11-028].
Warn with @deprecated in a minor release, ship codemods, drop it in the next major (Polaris) [S-L11-100].

questions.ask: How should you mark each component's status, number its versions, and retire old ones?
questions.example: Show a changelog entry with a deprecation and its codemod.
questions.why: Clear status labels and version numbers protect the teams that use your components. Breaking changes without warning wear away their trust [DC-L11-13, DC-L11-14, DC-L11-15].
questions.default: status-3, semver-library, deprecation-polaris with at least one release cycle of notice; release notes every release (the most common ritual, 56%)
questions.preview: status badges in the catalog and a sample changelog.
questions.use_avoid: pair every removal with a migration path; avoid breaking changes in minor releases [DC-L11-14, DC-L11-15].

questions.question: What problem is the system solving, and how will you know it worked?

options.label: Biggest problem
options.effect: inconsistency, speed, accessibility, rebrand, AI output drift, multi-platform parity [S-L11-083].

options.label: Design use and code use (Figma analytics; a scanner like Omlet or react-scanner) [S-L11-035, S-L11-037, S-L11-039].
A survey every quarter on how happy people are with it [S-L11-030].
Stage of growth
options.effect: building v1, growing adoption, surviving the teenage years, evolving (Sparkbox) [S-L11-033].

questions.ask: What problem hurts most today, and how will you measure whether the system helped?
questions.example: Show an adoption dashboard mock with the three starting metrics.
questions.why: The problem you are solving sets how you measure success. Most teams measure how much the system is used, but only 5% measure return on investment (ROI) [DC-L11-20; S-L11-030].
questions.default: design adoption, code adoption and a quarterly survey; most builder users are at stage 1
questions.preview: the metrics dashboard mock.
questions.use_avoid: add speed or ROI studies only when leadership asks; avoid vanity counts of components [DC-L11-20].

questions.question: How will you announce the system and communicate changes?

options.label: Release notes (56% of teams) [S-L11-030].
Office hours (33%) [S-L11-030].
Training, pairing, success stories (Frost) [S-L11-002].

questions.ask: How will you tell people about the system and about each change?
questions.example: Show a release-note template filled from a recent change.
questions.why: How you share changes matters: only 39% of teams are happy with how changes to their design system are shared [DC-L11-22; S-L11-030].
questions.default: release notes, a public roadmap and a support channel
questions.preview: the release-note template.
questions.use_avoid: use changelogs that name the migration; avoid silent releases [DC-L11-22].

questions.question: Which assistive tools must you test on each device, and who owns accessibility?

options.label: VoiceOver on Apple, TalkBack on Android phone, Wear and TV, NVDA/JAWS on web [S-L14-080, S-L10-072].
Switch Control, Voice Control, Full Keyboard Access, Dwell Control [S-L14-079, S-L14-007].
Largest text
options.effect: Dynamic Type AX5, Android 200%, watch 140% [S-L10-011, S-L10-071].

questions.ask: On each kind of device you ship, which screen readers, control tools and text sizes will you test?
questions.example: Show the generated test matrix for the chosen platforms.
questions.why: Automated checks find only about 30% of issues. If a kind of device gets full support, its assistive tools need full support too [DC-L14-14; S-L11-093].
questions.control: matrix (device class x assistive tech) + text (owner)
questions.default: one screen reader, one motor alternative and the largest text size per shipped device class; a named accessibility owner (44% of teams lack a specialist)
questions.preview: the test matrix with pass/untested status per cell.
questions.use_avoid: use manual assistive-technology testing on every release candidate; avoid treating automated scans as compliance [DC-L11-19, DC-L14-14].

questions.question: How should the system leave the builder?

options.label: Copy snippets (Radix "Copy Theme", Utopia CSS) [S-L16-323, S-L16-341].
A one-line install command from a URL (tweakcn via shadcn) [S-L16-333, S-L16-328].
Token files (Leonardo "Copy Tokens") [S-L16-338].
A pull request to the repository [DC-L16-12].
Push to Figma or Paper through MCP [S-L16-002, S-L16-020].
Make the builder's generator an MCP tool that AI can call (Leonardo's example) [S-L16-338].

questions.ask: In what forms should the system leave the builder: code, a command, files, a pull request, or Figma?
questions.example: Show the export menu with one command per channel (for example `npx shadcn@latest add <url>`).
questions.why: Engineers need the output in a form they already use. It can be a snippet, an install command, a token file, a pull request or a design file [DC-L16-12].
questions.default: all six from one menu
questions.preview: the export menu and file tree.
questions.use_avoid: use one canonical source for every channel (Q-tool-01); avoid channels that fork the source [DC-L16-02].

questions.question: Where do docs live, and what goes on each component page?

options.label: Figma plus Storybook (69% and 61% of teams) [S-L11-030].
A docs tool (zeroheight, Supernova), when people who don't code write the docs [S-L11-088].
A custom site (Material, Carbon) [S-L11-088].
Page template
options.effect: live demo, accessibility status, when to use and not, anatomy, content rules, behaviors, per-variant guidance (Carbon Usage tab; M3 Overview/Specs/Guidelines/Accessibility) [S-L11-090, S-L08-033].

questions.ask: Where should the docs live, and what should each component's page show?
questions.example: Show the generated Button page.
questions.why: Docs are how teams learn when to use each piece, and when not to. The core that systems share is usage advice, live examples, API and accessibility [DC-L11-17, DC-L11-18; L09 A1 row 9].
questions.default: a generated site with the Carbon-style template plus "when not to use" and a changelog, and an llms.txt or MCP twin; docs complete is part of "done"
questions.preview: a generated component page.
questions.use_avoid: use generated "use it for / avoid it for" notes from this questionnaire on every page; avoid docs that repeat props without guidance [DC-L11-18].

questions.question: How should AI coding tools read the system?

options.label: An MCP server (Figma MCP at mcp.figma.com; Storybook MCP; shadcn MCP) [S-L11-041, S-L11-044, S-L11-045].
DESIGN.md plus DTCG files [S-L11-047].
llms.txt and Markdown twins of docs (Cloudscape, Geist) [S-L11-048; L09 A1 row 10].
Rules files for AI agents (from Figma's create_design_system_rules) [S-L11-041].
A component registry (shadcn) [S-L11-045].

questions.ask: How should AI coding tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Cursor read your system?
questions.example: Show a DESIGN.md excerpt and an agent's generated button using the tokens.
questions.why: 59% of teams say some UI gets built around their design system. Channels made for AI agents make the UI they generate follow it [DC-L11-23; S-L11-031].
questions.default: at least one live channel (MCP) and one file channel (DESIGN.md + DTCG), guidelines as many short structured files
questions.default_source: card heuristic [DC-L11-23]; L09 shared pattern row 10 (12 of 25 systems).
questions.preview: the agent-facing files and a sample agent answer.
questions.use_avoid: use evals to check agents follow the files; avoid assuming docs changes alone steer agents [DC-L11-23; S-L11-108].

questions.question: How should the system check that people and agents follow it?

options.label: Lint rules shipped with the tokens, like target size, labels and one main button [DC-L11-24; L13 E3].
Scans that catch raw colors and one-off components (Lovable) [S-L11-053].
Drift detection at the docs layer (zeroheight MCP) [S-L11-104].
Tests that measure how well AI agents follow the system (evals) [S-L11-108].

questions.ask: How should we catch screens that break the system's rules, whether a person or AI made them?
questions.example: Show a lint result: "raw hex #3b82f6, use color.bg.accent".
questions.why: When AI agents built with a design system, lint rules and structured docs cut accessibility errors. They fell from 5.1 to 0.6 per round in Sanity's evals [DC-L11-24; L13 E3].
questions.default: lint-rules plus evals
questions.preview: the lint report for the preview screen.
questions.use_avoid: use lint errors for Tier A rules and warnings for context-dependent ones (L13 E1); avoid automating the misapplied laws in L13 E2 (no seven-item caps) [L13 E1, E2].

questions.question: How strict should the builder's critique be?

options.label: Silent
options.effect: only automatic rules apply [DC-L15-11].

options.label: Coach
options.effect: inline messages tied to a goal, each with a one-click fix (NN/g goal-linked critique) [S-L15-075].

options.label: Strict
options.effect: block export on contrast, multiple primaries and undersized targets; warn on the rest [DC-L15-11].

options.label: Plus a panel that scores how complex and colorful it is [S-L15-047].

questions.ask: Should I give tips as you go, stay quiet, or block export on serious problems like contrast?
questions.example: Show one coach message: "Two primary buttons in this group; make one secondary."
questions.why: Tips that name the design principle teach people the words for it. Strict mode stops export when something fails badly [DC-L15-11; S-L15-070].
questions.default: coach for engineers exploring; strict for teams shipping to production
questions.preview: the preview screen with messages at each level.
questions.use_avoid: accessibility failures are at least warnings in every mode; avoid silent mode for production exports [DC-L15-11].

questions.question: How should AI edits and variations work?

options.label: AI changes arrive as patches you review, with before and after views [DC-L16-04].
Your own edits wait, then save all at once (Figma Make) [S-L16-026].
Lock what you like and shuffle the rest, for every setting (shadcn create, Realtime Colors) [S-L16-327, S-L16-335].
A "show 6" grid of versions on the same sample screen [DC-L16-05].

questions.ask: When the AI changes your design, how should you review it and try other versions?
questions.example: Show a "show 6 variations" grid with two locked parameters.
questions.why: Your own edits do exactly what you set, and AI edits come as patches you review, so you keep control and trust. Lock-and-shuffle tries new options without losing what you like [DC-L16-04, DC-L16-05].
questions.default: patches, lock-shuffle and show-6; vary only what is not locked
questions.preview: the variation grid.
questions.use_avoid: use variations for open, taste-driven questions (color, type, radius); avoid shuffling locked or accessibility-bound values [DC-L16-05].

questions.question: Should the builder fix shapes that look wrong to the eye, even when the math is right?

options.label: Exact math only
options.effect: exact values [DC-L15-10].

options.label: Fix known cases for you
options.effect: area-matched shapes (circle 112.84%), Material keylines, centroid centering, concentric nested radii [S-L15-058, S-L15-059].

options.label: Suggest only [DC-L15-10].

questions.ask: How should the builder handle shapes that look off to the eye, like icon sizes and nested corners?
questions.example: Show a circle icon at 100% vs 112.84% of a square's box.
questions.why: Exact sizes can look wrong: a circle looks smaller than a square in the same box. The known fixes have formulas [DC-L15-10; S-L15-058].
questions.default: auto-known for generated assets, suggest for custom assets
questions.preview: before/after pairs for each correction.
questions.use_avoid: use formulas where they exist; avoid correcting brand assets without approval [DC-L15-10].

auto_applied.rule the builder applies: Backgrounds edge-to-edge; interactive content inside platform insets plus the layout margin; nothing on a foldable hinge
Safe zones per device: nothing to read or select in the outer 5% on TV; percentage margins on round watches; car targets 24dp from edges
Nested radius: inner = max(outer - padding, smallest non-zero radius); warn on equal nested radii
Layer order as named layers spaced by 100: base < sticky < dropdown < overlay/scrim < modal < popover/tooltip < toast < skip link; no hard-coded z-index
Every translucent token ships with an opaque twin, honoring Reduce Transparency and `prefers-reduced-transparency`
Images always reserve their final box; neutral placeholder fill; skeletons only on container components
Chart chrome (titles, ticks, gridlines, legends) maps to existing text and border tokens; chart-specific tokens only for marks and interaction
Every chart gets an insight title, direct labels or shape-coded legend, a text summary and "view as table"
Docs and generated pages use a heading per section, front-loaded paragraphs, bullets for 3+ items
Each interactive component documents trigger, rules, feedback, loops and modes plus its state list
Text survives WCAG 1.4.12 overrides (line height 1.5x, paragraph 2x, letter 0.12x, word 0.16x); no fixed-height text boxes
Every text style is contrast-checked in every mode; below 18.5px bold / 24px regular it needs 4.5:1

disagreements.question: Q-plat-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Default platforms: L10 recommends web + iOS + Android phones with large-screen layouts [DC-L10-01]; survey data shows 94% of systems support web and about a third support native [S-L11-030]; L09 finds web-only most common [L09 A2 row 10].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Default to web, and show the native options with what each adds (chrome, units, targets).

disagreements.question: Q-tool-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Source of truth: L16 and L11 favor the builder's own model [DC-L16-02, DC-L11-16]; L07 favors DTCG JSON in git [DC-L07-08]; the 2026 practitioner majority says code [COMMUNITY-SIGNAL via DC-L11-16].
disagreements.what the builder should present: All four options with the drift trade-off; default builder model compiled to DTCG and code.

disagreements.question: Q-form-02
disagreements.the disagreement: Disabled submit: Carbon disables on short forms [S-L08-106]; Atlassian never disables [S-L08-085]; Material's disabled components are not focusable [S-L08-095]. BOARD also flags tooltips on disabled controls as contested.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Offer both policies; default never-disable with `aria-disabled` and helper text.

disagreements.question: Q-form-04
disagreements.the disagreement: Toasts: Primer ships none [S-L08-098]; Carbon, Atlassian and Material ship them [S-L08-079, S-L08-011, S-L08-008].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Three options; default toasts only for low-stakes results with undo.

disagreements.question: Q-form-02
disagreements.the disagreement: Validation timing: GOV.UK validates on submit [S-L08-077]; NN/g research favors on-blur for most inputs [S-L13-100].
disagreements.what the builder should present: On-blur for format checks, on submit for the rest, with the summary pattern.

disagreements.question: Q-motion-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Motion default: Material's expressive spring scheme is its default for most products [DC-L10-14; S-L10-024]; Carbon and L04 default to productive motion with bounce at or below 0.2 [DC-L04-19].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Two-mode default; springs as an explicit choice; productive cap for high-trust products.

disagreements.question: Q-state-03
disagreements.the disagreement: Focus ring: Material uses 3px [S-L04-003]; Atlassian and Primer use 2px [S-L04-016, S-L04-024]; BOARD's L13 note flags a Figma article's 3px claim as contradicting WCAG, pending the V1 verification pass.
disagreements.what the builder should present: 2px default with an offset, 3px as an option; both must meet 3:1.

disagreements.question: Q-type-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Typeface default: L02 says the system stack for productivity tools [DC-L02-01]; L09 says Inter or the system stack [DC-L09-05].
disagreements.what the builder should present: System stack by default for tools, open-neutral (Inter) as the one-click alternative.

disagreements.question: Q-type-08, Q-aud-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Body size: L02's web default is 14px UI text [DC-L02-08]; L09's regular preset is 16px [L09 A1 row 8]. They agree once density is known.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Tie body size to the density answer instead of one fixed default.

disagreements.question: Q-token-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Tiers: L07 says two tiers with component tokens only when needed [DC-L07-01]; L09 and L01 say three tiers with the component tier optional [L09 A1 row 1; DC-L01-26]. Same structure, different counting.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Present it as "primitive -> semantic, component tokens on demand".

disagreements.question: Q-color-17
disagreements.the disagreement: Contrast method: WCAG 2.2 is the enforceable standard; Radix and Geist use APCA; WCAG 3 is still a draft [DC-L01-22; BOARD L01 note].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Enforce WCAG 2.2, show APCA as advisory.

disagreements.question: Q-color-06
disagreements.the disagreement: Dynamic color: Material pushes dynamic color [DC-L01-21]; brand-led consumer apps keep fixed brand color, and iOS has no equivalent [DC-L10-05].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Per-platform choice; brand-critical and status colors always fixed.

disagreements.question: Q-space-01
disagreements.the disagreement: Base unit: 8 (Carbon, Atlassian, Material, Spectrum naming) vs 4 (Fluent, Polaris, Primer, Tailwind) [DC-L03-01].
disagreements.what the builder should present: "4 as the grid, 8 as the rhythm" as a reconciling default.

disagreements.question: Q-shape-03
disagreements.the disagreement: Pills: Material and Spectrum 2 use pills widely [DC-L09-01]; Carbon v12 moved tags away from pills [S-L04-031]; Atlassian reserves full radius for people [S-L04-016].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Pill as an option per component role; people = full circle by default.

disagreements.question: Asset hooks
disagreements.the disagreement: Fallback order: L17's policy puts "commission a designer" before open libraries [DC-L17-04]; the icon and typeface cards default to open libraries first [DC-L05-01, DC-L02-01].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Icons and typefaces lead with open libraries (they are tool-assisted blocks); identity assets (logo, app icon, illustration, photography, sound) lead with commissioning.

disagreements.question: Quick mode
disagreements.the disagreement: L17 says owner-input blocks are never auto-decided [DC-L17-08]; Quick mode asks only 10 questions, so scope, principles and similar owner inputs take defaults.
disagreements.what the builder should present: Quick records them as "assumed" and lists them for confirmation at the end (`meta.quick_mode_assumed_owner_inputs`).

disagreements.question: Q-voice-03
disagreements.the disagreement: Capitalization: sentence case everywhere (Microsoft, Atlassian) vs title-case headings (Mailchimp) vs per element (Apple) [DC-L06-20].
disagreements.what the builder should present: Three options; sentence case by default.
